title.zh: 卷二百八十七 列傳第四十六 楊礪 宋湜 王嗣宗 李昌齡 趙安仁 陳彭年
title.en: Volume 287 Biographies 46: Yang Li, Song Shi, Wang Sizong, Li Changling, Zhao Anren, Chen Pengnian
title.raw: 卷二百八十七 列傳第四十六 楊礪 宋湜 王嗣宗 李昌齡 趙安仁 陳彭年 Volume 287 Biographies 46: Yang Li, Song Shi, Wang Sizong, Li Changling, Zhao Anren, Chen Pengnian

sentences.zh: 楊礪，字汝礪，京兆鄠人。

translations.literal: Yang Li, style name Ruli, a man of Hu in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Li, courtesy name Ruli, was a native of Hu in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖守信，唐山南西道節度、同平章事，本宦官復恭假子也。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shouxin was Tang Shannan West Circuit military commissioner and Tongpingzhangshi; originally he was the foster son of the eunuch Fugong.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shouxin had served as military governor of the Shannan West circuit and as Tongpingzhangshi under Tang; he had originally been the foster son of the eunuch Fugong.

sentences.zh: 祖知禮，後唐均州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhili was Later Tang prefect of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhili had been prefect of Jun Prefecture under Later Tang.

sentences.zh: 父仁儼，入蜀仕王氏，為丹棱令。

translations.literal: His father Renyan entered Shu and served the Wang clan, becoming magistrate of Danling.
translations.idiomatic: His father Renyan had entered Shu and served the Wang regime, becoming magistrate of Danling.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，補渭南主簿，累遷永和令。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, he was appointed Weinan registrar and was repeatedly promoted to magistrate of Yonghe.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified, he was appointed recorder of Weinan and was eventually promoted to magistrate of Yonghe.

sentences.zh: 礪，建隆中舉進士甲科。

translations.literal: Li, in the Jianlong era, passed the jinshi examination in the first class.
translations.idiomatic: Li passed the jinshi examination in the first class during the Jianlong era.

sentences.zh: 父喪，絕水漿數日。

translations.literal: When his father died, he abstained from food and drink for several days.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died, he went without food or drink for several days.

sentences.zh: 服除，以祿不足養母，閑居無仕進意，鄉舊移書敦諭，礪乃赴官。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, because his salary was insufficient to support his mother, he lived in retirement with no wish to advance; old acquaintances of the district sent letters urging him, and only then did Li take office.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, his salary was too small to support his mother, so he lived at home with no ambition for office; old friends in the district wrote urging him on, and only then did Li accept a post.

sentences.zh: 解褐鳳州團練推官，歲餘，又以母疾棄官。

translations.literal: Upon first taking office he was Fengzhou training command military administration secretary; after more than a year he again resigned because of his mother's illness.
translations.idiomatic: On entering office he was made military administration secretary of the Fengzhou training command; after a little more than a year he resigned again because his mother was ill.

sentences.zh: 開寶九年，詣闕獻書，召試學士院，授隴州防禦推官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Kaibao he went to court and presented a book; summoned for examination at the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, he was appointed Longzhou defense administration secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Kaibao he went to the capital and presented a book; after being examined at the Hanlin Academy he was appointed defense administration secretary of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 入遷光祿寺丞，丁內艱，起就職。

translations.literal: He entered service and was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; when his wife's parent died he was recalled to office.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; when his wife's parent died he left mourning and returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 久之，轉秘書丞，改屯田員外郎、知鄂州，以善政聞。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to secretary of the Secretariat and changed to outer bureau director of the Ministry of Revenue fields and acting prefect of Ezhou, becoming known for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he became secretary of the Secretariat, then outer bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue and acting prefect of Ezhou, where he won a reputation for good government.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，真宗在襄邸，遷庫部，充記室參軍，賜金紫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong, when Zhenzong was at the Xiang residence, Li was moved to the treasury department, made staff recorder, and granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Duangong era, when Zhenzong was at the Xiang palace, Li was transferred to the treasury department, appointed staff recorder, and granted gold and purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 初，廣順中，周世宗節制澶州，礪贄文見之，館接數日。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Guangshun era, when Emperor Shizong of Zhou was in charge at Cangzhou, Li presented a literary gift and met him; he was lodged and received for several days.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Guangshun era, when the Zhou Emperor Shizong was stationed at Cangzhou, Li presented a literary work and was received; he was entertained as a guest for several days.

sentences.zh: 世宗入朝，礪處僧舍，夢古衣冠者曰：「汝能從乎？」

translations.literal: When Shizong went to court, Li was staying in a monks' lodging and dreamed that a man in ancient cap and robes said: "Can you follow?"
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong went to the capital, Li was staying in a monastery and dreamed that a man in ancient court dress said, "Will you come with me?"

sentences.zh: 礪隨往，睹宮衛若非人間，殿上王者秉珪南向，總三十餘。

translations.literal: Li followed, seeing palace guards as if not of the human world; on the hall kings holding scepters faced south, more than thirty in all.
translations.idiomatic: Li followed along and saw palace guards unlike anything in the mortal world; in the hall more than thirty kings holding jade scepters faced south.

sentences.zh: 礪升謁之，最上者前有案，置簿錄人姓名，礪見己名居首，因請示休咎。

translations.literal: Li went up to pay respects; before the highest one was a desk with a register of people's names—Li saw his own name at the head and therefore asked to be shown fortune or misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Li went forward to pay his respects; before the highest figure stood a desk with a register of names, and Li saw his own name at the top, so he asked what his fate would be.

sentences.zh: 王者曰：「我非汝師。」

translations.literal: The king said: "I am not your teacher."
translations.idiomatic: The king said, "I am not your teacher."

sentences.zh: 指一人曰：「此來和天尊，異日汝主也，當問之。」

translations.literal: He pointed to a man and said: "This is the Laihe Heavenly Lord; in days to come he will be your lord—you should ask him."
translations.idiomatic: He pointed to someone and said, "This is the Laihe Heavenly Lord; one day he will be your sovereign—you should ask him."

sentences.zh: 其人笑曰：「此去四十年，汝功成，予名亦顯矣。」

translations.literal: That man smiled and said: "From now forty years—when you achieve merit, my name will also become illustrious."
translations.idiomatic: That man smiled and said, "Forty years from now, when you have achieved success, my name too will be renowned."

sentences.zh: 礪再拜，寤而誌之。

translations.literal: Li bowed twice, awoke, and recorded it.
translations.idiomatic: Li bowed twice, woke, and wrote the dream down.

sentences.zh: 礪初名勵，以籍作礪，遂改之。

translations.literal: Li's original name was Li; because the register had Li written as Li, he changed it.
translations.idiomatic: Li had originally been named Li; because the household register gave the character for his name as Li, he adopted that form.

sentences.zh: 至是，受命謁見藩府，歸謂子曰：「吾今見襄王儀貌，即所夢來和天尊也。」

translations.literal: At this time, having received orders to pay a visit at the princely residence, on returning he told his son: "I have now seen the Prince of Xiang's bearing—it is the Laihe Heavenly Lord of my dream."
translations.idiomatic: Now, after being ordered to call at the prince's residence, he returned and told his son, "I have just seen the Prince of Xiang's appearance—it is the Laihe Heavenly Lord from my dream."

sentences.zh: 遷水部郎中。

translations.literal: He was moved to bureau director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 真宗尹開封，礪為推官。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong administered Kaifeng, Li was his administration secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong governed Kaifeng, Li served as his administration secretary.

sentences.zh: 真宗嘗問礪：「何年及第？」

translations.literal: Zhenzong once asked Li: "In what year did you pass the examination?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong once asked Li, "In what year did you pass the examinations?"

sentences.zh: 礪唯唯不對。

translations.literal: Li only murmured and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Li only murmured and would not answer.

sentences.zh: 後知其唱名第一，自悔失問，謂礪不以科名自伐，甚重之。

translations.literal: Later learning that he had been called first at the roll, he regretted the missed question and said that Li did not boast of his examination rank—he valued him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Later, learning that Li had been announced first at the palace examination, he regretted having asked the wrong question and said that Li did not flaunt his examination rank; he esteemed him all the more.

sentences.zh: 儲宮建，兼右諭德，轉度支郎中。

translations.literal: When the heir apparent was established, Li concurrently served as right mentor and was transferred to bureau director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent was established, Li also served as right mentor of the heir apparent and was transferred to bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 即位，拜給事中、判吏部銓。

translations.literal: On accession he was appointed supervising censor and given charge of the Ministry of Personnel selection.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong took the throne, Li was appointed supervising censor and put in charge of personnel selection at the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召入翰林為學士。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned into the Hanlin as academician.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy as an academician.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，知貢舉，俄拜工部侍郎、樞密副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping he supervised the metropolitan examinations; soon he was appointed vice minister of Works and deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianping era he supervised the civil service examinations; soon afterward he was appointed vice minister of Works and deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年，卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: In the second year he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he died, at the age of sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 真宗軫悼，謂宰相曰：「礪介直清苦，方當任用，遽此淪謝。」

translations.literal: Zhenzong was deeply grieved and told the chief ministers: "Li was upright and austere, just when he should have been employed—suddenly he has perished thus."
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong was deeply grieved and told his chief ministers, "Li was upright and lived in hardship; he was just the man to employ—and now he is suddenly gone."

sentences.zh: 即冒雨臨其喪。

translations.literal: He immediately went in the rain to his mourning hall.
translations.idiomatic: He went at once through the rain to Li's mourning hall.

sentences.zh: 礪僦舍委巷中，乘輿不能進，步至其第，嗟憫久之。

translations.literal: Li rented a house in a winding lane; the imperial carriage could not enter, so he walked to the residence and sighed in compassion for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Li had rented a house in a narrow back lane, and the imperial carriage could not pass; the emperor walked to the door and sighed in pity for a long while.

sentences.zh: 廢朝，贈兵部尚書，中使護葬。

translations.literal: Court was suspended; he was posthumously made minister of War, and a palace envoy supervised the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning was declared; Li was posthumously made minister of War, and a palace envoy supervised his burial.

sentences.zh: 礪為文尚繁，無師法，每詩一題或數十篇。

translations.literal: Li's writing favored prolixity, without masterly method; for each poetic topic he might write dozens of pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Li's writing tended toward prolixity and lacked disciplined craft; for a single poetic topic he might compose dozens of poems.

sentences.zh: 在翰林，制誥迂怪，見者哂之。

translations.literal: In the Hanlin, his edicts were tortuous and strange; those who saw them laughed.
translations.idiomatic: While in the Hanlin, his edicts were convoluted and eccentric, and those who read them smiled.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 子嶠至祠部郎中；

translations.literal: His son Qiao rose to bureau director of the Ministry of Rites;
translations.idiomatic: His son Qiao rose to bureau director in the Ministry of Rites;

sentences.zh: 嶧至太常博士；

translations.literal: Yi rose to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: Yi rose to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 峭至太子中舍。

translations.literal: Qiao rose to middle household attendant of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao rose to middle household attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 少子嵎，至道初與張庶凝刊校真宗儲邸書籍，真宗即位，皆賜進士出身、直史館。

translations.literal: The youngest son Yu, at the beginning of Zhidao together with Zhang Shuning collated and proofread the books of Zhenzong's princely residence; when Zhenzong acceded, both were granted jinshi status and direct appointment to the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son Yu, early in the Zhidao era, collated the books of Zhenzong's princely residence together with Zhang Shuning; when Zhenzong took the throne, both were granted jinshi status and appointment to the History Office.

sentences.zh: 嵎至祠部郎中，庶凝至太常丞。

translations.literal: Yu rose to bureau director of the Ministry of Rites; Shuning rose to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yu rose to bureau director in the Ministry of Rites; Shuning rose to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 宋湜，字持正，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Song Shi, style name Chizheng, a man of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shi, courtesy name Chizheng, was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖擇，牟平令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Ze was magistrate of Mouping.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Ze had been magistrate of Mouping.

sentences.zh: 祖讚，萬年令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zan was magistrate of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zan had been magistrate of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 父溫故，晉天福中進士，至左補闕；

translations.literal: His father Wengu, a jinshi in the Tianfu era of Jin, rose to left remonstrance official;
translations.idiomatic: His father Wengu, a jinshi of the Jin Tianfu era, rose to left remonstrance official;

sentences.zh: 弟溫舒，亦進士，至職方員外郎，兄弟皆有時名。

translations.literal: His younger brother Wenshu was also a jinshi and rose to outer bureau director of the Ministry of War; the brothers both had contemporary renown.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wenshu was also a jinshi and rose to outer bureau director in the Ministry of War; both brothers enjoyed renown in their day.

sentences.zh: 湜幼警悟，早孤，與兄泌勵志篤學，事母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Shi from youth was keen and perceptive; orphaned early, with his elder brother Bi he resolved to study diligently and was known for filial service to his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was clever from childhood and lost his father early; with his elder brother Bi he devoted himself to study and was known for his filial care of his mother.

sentences.zh: 溫舒典耀州，湜侍行，代作箋奏，詞敏而麗。

translations.literal: When Wenshu administered Yaozhou, Shi accompanied him and drafted memorials in his place; the language was quick and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenshu was prefect of Yao Prefecture, Shi accompanied him and drafted memorials on his behalf; the prose was swift and polished.

sentences.zh: 溫舒拊背曰：「此兒真國器，恨吾兄不及見也。」

translations.literal: Wenshu patted his back and said: "This boy is truly state timber—I regret that my elder brother did not live to see it."
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu clapped him on the back and said, "This boy is truly material for the state—I only regret that my elder brother did not live to see it."

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年進士，釋褐將作監丞、通判梓州榷鹽院，就遷右贊善大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he passed the jinshi examination; upon first office he was vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and transit judge of the Zizhou salt monopoly office, and was soon promoted to right mentor grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo; on entering office he was made vice director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and transit judge of the Zizhou salt monopoly office, and was soon promoted to right mentor grandee.

sentences.zh: 宋準薦其文，拜著作郎、直史館，賜緋。

translations.literal: Song Zhun recommended his writing; he was appointed drafting official and direct appointment to the History Office, and granted scarlet.
translations.idiomatic: Song Zhun recommended his writing; he was appointed drafting official and given a direct appointment to the History Office, with scarlet robes.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，以右補闕知制誥，與王化基、李沆並命，仍賜白金五百兩、錢五十萬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi he was made right remonstrance official with charge of edicts, appointed together with Wang Huaji and Li Hang, and also granted five hundred taels of white gold and five hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi he was made right remonstrance official with charge of drafting edicts, appointed together with Wang Huaji and Li Hang, and also granted five hundred taels of white gold and five hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 加戶部員外郎，與蘇易簡同知貢舉，俄判刑部，賜金紫。

translations.literal: He was added outer bureau director of the Ministry of Revenue; with Su Yijian he jointly supervised the examinations; soon he was given charge of the Ministry of Justice and granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: He was made outer bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue and, with Su Yijian, jointly supervised the civil service examinations; soon he was put in charge of the Ministry of Justice and granted gold and purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，祅尼道安訟大理斷獄不當，湜坐累，降均州團練副使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua the heterodox nun Dao'an sued over improper judgment of a case in the Court of Judicial Review; Shi was implicated and demoted to deputy military training commissioner of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua the heterodox nun Dao'an brought suit over an improper judgment in the Court of Judicial Review; Shi was implicated and demoted to deputy military training commissioner of Jun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時母老，湜留其室奉養。

translations.literal: At the time his mother was old; Shi left his quarters to support her.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was then elderly, and Shi left his post to care for her at home.

sentences.zh: 移汝州，與王禹偁並召入，為禮部員外郎、直昭文館。

translations.literal: Transferred to Ruzhou, he and Wang Yucheng were both summoned in and made outer bureau director of the Ministry of Rites with direct appointment to the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: After transfer to Ru Prefecture, he and Wang Yucheng were both recalled to court and made outer bureau director in the Ministry of Rites with a direct appointment to the Zhaowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 五年，以職方員外郎再知制誥、判集賢院，知銀臺、通進、封駮司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, as outer bureau director of the Ministry of War he again had charge of edicts and was given the Jixian Academy, and supervised the Yintai, Tongjin, and Fengbo offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, as outer bureau director in the Ministry of War he again drafted edicts and was put in charge of the Jixian Academy and the Yintai, Tongjin, and Fengbo offices.

sentences.zh: 至道元年，為翰林學士，知審官院、三班。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhidao he became Hanlin academician, with charge of the Bureau for Review of Appointments and the Three Classes.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhidao he became a Hanlin academician and was put in charge of the Bureau for Review of Appointments and the Three Classes.

sentences.zh: 又兼修國史、判昭文史館事，加兵部郎中。

translations.literal: He also concurrently compiled the national history and was given charge of Zhaowen Hall affairs, and was added bureau director of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped compile the national history and was put in charge of Zhaowen Hall affairs, and was promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded he was appointed secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong took the throne, Shi was appointed secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，起復。

translations.literal: When his wife's parent died he was recalled from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife's parent died he was recalled from mourning to office.

sentences.zh: 咸平元年冬，改給事中，充樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Xianping he was changed to supervising censor and made deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Xianping he was made supervising censor and deputy commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 真宗北巡，將次大名，以扈從軍列為行陣，親御鎧甲於中，諸王、樞密介胄以從，命湜與王顯分押後陣。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong toured the north and was about to halt at Daming, the escort troops were arrayed in battle order; he personally donned armor in the center, princes and Bureau of Military Affairs officials in armor followed, and Shi and Wang Xian were ordered to command the rear separately.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong toured the north and was about to halt at Daming, the escort troops were drawn up in battle array; the emperor himself wore armor in the center, with princes and Bureau officials in armor following, and Shi and Wang Xian were ordered to command the rear guard separately.

sentences.zh: 駐蹕數日，常召見便殿，方奏事，疾作仆地。

translations.literal: After halting for several days he was often summoned to the side hall; while reporting on affairs an illness struck and he fell to the ground.
translations.idiomatic: After several days' halt he was often summoned to the side hall; while reporting on business he was seized by illness and collapsed.

sentences.zh: 內侍掖出，太醫診視，撫問相繼，以疾亟聞。

translations.literal: Palace attendants helped him out; imperial physicians examined him; inquiries followed one after another, and word was sent that the illness was grave.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants helped him out; imperial physicians examined him; inquiries followed in succession, and word was sent that his illness was grave.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，真宗臨視，許以先歸，賜衾褥，曰：「此朕嘗御者，雖故暗，亦足禦道途之寒。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year Zhenzong visited him in person, permitted him to return home first, and granted bedding, saying: "These I have used; though old and dim, they are enough to ward off the cold of the road."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Zhenzong visited him in person, allowed him to return home ahead, and gave him bedding, saying, "These I have used myself; though worn and faded, they will be enough to keep off the cold on the road."

sentences.zh: 又遣內侍護送供帳，至澶州，卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: He also sent palace attendants to escort his supplies; at Cangzhou he died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent palace attendants to escort his traveling equipment; at Cangzhou Shi died, at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 廢朝，贈吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Court was suspended; he was posthumously made vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning was declared; he was posthumously made vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 以子綸為太祝、純為奉禮郎；

translations.literal: His son Lun was made libationer; Chun was made court gentleman of offerings;
translations.idiomatic: His son Lun was made libationer and Chun was made court gentleman of offerings;

sentences.zh: 弟某為光祿寺丞、湛為大理寺丞；

translations.literal: a younger brother was made vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Zhan was made vice director of the Court of Judicial Review;
translations.idiomatic: a younger brother was made vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Zhan was made vice director of the Court of Judicial Review;

sentences.zh: 侄孫選同學究出身。

translations.literal: a nephew's grandson Xuan was granted tongxue juren status.
translations.idiomatic: a grandnephew Xuan was granted tongxue juren status.

sentences.zh: 真宗再幸河朔，追悼之，加贈刑部尚書，諡曰忠定。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong again visited Heshuo he mourned him posthumously, added posthumous gift of minister of Justice, and gave the posthumous title Zhongding.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong again visited the north he mourned him afresh, posthumously promoted him to minister of Justice, and gave him the posthumous title Zhongding (Loyal and Settled).

sentences.zh: 湜風貌秀整，有醞藉，器識沖遠，好學，美文詞，善談論飲謔，曉音律，妙於奕棋。

translations.literal: Shi's bearing was handsome and orderly, with cultured reserve; his capacity and insight were lofty and remote; he loved learning, fine literary composition, skilled talk and banter over drink, understood musical pitch, and was masterly at go.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was handsome and well composed, with cultivated reserve; his judgment was lofty and far-reaching; he loved learning and fine writing, was skilled at conversation and witty banter over wine, understood music, and was a master of go.

sentences.zh: 筆法遒媚，書帖之出，人多傳效。

translations.literal: His brushwork was forceful and graceful; when calligraphic models issued from him many people copied them.
translations.idiomatic: His calligraphy was vigorous and elegant, and when his models circulated many people imitated them.

sentences.zh: 喜引重後進有名者，又好趨人之急，當世士流，翕然宗仰之。

translations.literal: He delighted in promoting younger men of name and also in rushing to others' urgent needs; men of the age in official circles all at once revered him.
translations.idiomatic: He liked to advance talented younger men and was quick to help others in need; men of the age in official circles looked up to him as one.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 湜兄泌，太平興國二年進士，至起居郎、直史館、越王府記室參軍。

translations.literal: Shi's elder brother Bi, a jinshi in the second year of Taiping Xingguo, rose to palace attendant, direct History Office appointment, and staff recorder of the Prince of Yue's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's elder brother Bi, a jinshi of the second year of Taiping Xingguo, rose to palace attendant, direct appointment to the History Office, and staff recorder of the Prince of Yue's residence.

sentences.zh: 溫舒三子，沆、澥、濤。

translations.literal: Wenshu had three sons: Hang, Xie, and Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu had three sons: Hang, Xie, and Tao.

sentences.zh: 沆，剛率，喜談兵。

translations.literal: Hang was stern and forthright and delighted in discussing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Hang was stern and blunt and liked to talk about military affairs.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年進士，歷左正言、京西轉運使、度支判官。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, he served as left rectifier, transport commissioner of the Jingxi circuit, and revenue disbursement judge.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo, he served as left rectifier, transport commissioner of the Jingxi circuit, and revenue disbursement judge.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，呂蒙正罷相，沆坐親黨，貶宜州團練副使，起為太子中允，換如京副使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua, when Lü Mengzheng was dismissed as chief minister, Hang was implicated as a kinsman and demoted to deputy military training commissioner of Yizhou; recalled as middle palace attendant and exchanged to deputy commissioner of the Capital Transport Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua, when Lü Mengzheng was dismissed as chief minister, Hang was implicated as a partisan and demoted to deputy military training commissioner of Yi Prefecture; he was later recalled as middle palace attendant and transferred to deputy commissioner of the Capital Transport Office.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，遣與梅詢使西京為安撫使，未行，罷為環慶路都監。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era he was sent with Mei Xun as pacification commissioner to the Western Capital; before departing he was dismissed and made overall controller of the Huanqing circuit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era he was dispatched with Mei Xun as pacification commissioner to the Western Capital; before he could depart he was reassigned as overall controller of the Huanqing circuit.

sentences.zh: 與知環州張從古擅發兵襲敵，不與部署叶謀，又士卒有死傷者，責授供奉官。

translations.literal: With Zhang Conggu, prefect of Huanzhou, he launched troops on his own authority to raid the enemy, did not consult the deployment commissioner Ye Mou, and soldiers were killed and wounded; he was punished by appointment as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Zhang Conggu, prefect of Huan Prefecture, he launched troops on his own authority to raid the enemy without consulting deployment commissioner Ye Mou, and some soldiers were killed or wounded; he was reduced to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 後為文思副使、京西提點刑獄，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was deputy commissioner of the Literary Reflection Office and judicial intendant of the Jingxi circuit, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as deputy commissioner of the Literary Reflection Office and judicial intendant of the Jingxi circuit, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 澥有清節，居長安不仕，與种放、魏野遊，多篇什酬唱。

translations.literal: Xie had pure integrity, lived in Chang'an without taking office, traveled with Zhong Fang and Wei Ye, and exchanged many poems.
translations.idiomatic: Xie lived with integrity, remained in Chang'an without taking office, associated with Zhong Fang and Wei Ye, and exchanged many poems with them.

sentences.zh: 濤，端拱二年進士，歷殿中丞、知襄城縣，以政績聞，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: Tao, a jinshi in the second year of Duangong, served as palace administration director and prefect of Xiangcheng county, was known for administrative achievement, and was granted scarlet fish insignia.
translations.idiomatic: Tao, a jinshi of the second year of Duangong, served as palace administration director and magistrate of Xiangcheng county, won notice for his administration, and was granted scarlet fish insignia.

sentences.zh: 歷鹽鐵判官，累遷監察御史、知虢州。

translations.literal: He served as salt and iron judge and was repeatedly promoted to investigating censor and prefect of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as salt and iron judge and was eventually promoted to investigating censor and prefect of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 純及泌子緯皆至殿中丞。

translations.literal: Chun and Bi's son Wei both rose to palace administration director.
translations.idiomatic: Chun and Bi's son Wei both rose to palace administration director.

sentences.zh: 王嗣宗

translations.literal: Wang Sizong
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizong

sentences.zh: 王嗣宗，字希阮，汾州人。

translations.literal: Wang Sizong, style name Xiruan, a man of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizong, courtesy name Xiruan, was a native of Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖同節，寶鼎令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Tongjie was magistrate of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Tongjie had been magistrate of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 祖待價，汾州防禦推官。

translations.literal: His grandfather Daijia was Fenzhou defense administration secretary.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Daijia had been defense administration secretary of Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父夢證，成州軍事判官。

translations.literal: His father Mengzheng was military administration judge of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mengzheng had been military administration judge of Cheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗少力學自奮，遊京師，以文謁王祜，頗見優待。

translations.literal: Sizong from youth studied hard and urged himself on; traveling to the capital he presented his writing to Wang You and was quite well received.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong from youth studied hard and pushed himself forward; in the capital he presented his writing to Wang You and was treated with considerable favor.

sentences.zh: 開寶八年，登進士甲科，補秦州司寇參軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kaibao he passed the jinshi examination in the first class and was appointed Qinzhou judicial military adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Kaibao he passed the jinshi examination in the first class and was appointed judicial military adjutant of Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 侍御史路冲知州事，為政苛急，盜賊群起。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Lu Chong knew the prefectural affairs; his government was harsh and urgent, and bandits rose in groups.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Lu Chong was in charge of the prefecture; his government was harsh and severe, and bandits rose in bands.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗乘間極言其闕失，冲大怒，繫嗣宗於獄，又教無賴民被罪者訟嗣宗治獄枉濫。

translations.literal: Sizong seized an opportunity and spoke at length of his failings; Chong was greatly angered, bound Sizong in prison, and further incited ruffians who had been convicted to sue Sizong for abusive and arbitrary handling of prisoners in the jail.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong seized an opportunity to speak at length about his failings. Chong flew into a rage, imprisoned Sizong, and further incited convicted ruffians to bring suits accusing him of abusive and arbitrary conduct in the jail.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣殿中丞王廷範按之，具獲訟者誣罔狀，嗣宗乃得釋。

translations.literal: The court dispatched Palace Affairs director Wang Tingfan to investigate; he fully obtained the accusers' perjurious and deceptive condition, and only then was Sizong released.
translations.idiomatic: The court dispatched Palace Affairs director Wang Tingfan to investigate. He fully uncovered the accusers' perjury and deception, and only then was Sizong released.

sentences.zh: 太宗征河東，嗣宗陳邊事，召赴行在，授大理寺丞、通判睦州，改右贊善大夫、徙河州。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong campaigned against Hedong, Sizong submitted border affairs, was summoned to the imperial camp, appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review and Vice Prefect of Mu Prefecture, then changed to Right Advocate-in-Attendance and transferred to He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong campaigned against Hedong, Sizong submitted a report on border affairs and was summoned to the imperial camp. He was appointed Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review and Vice Prefect of Mu Prefecture, then promoted to Right Advocate-in-Attendance and transferred to He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太宗遣武德卒潛察遠方事，嗣宗械送京師，因奏曰：「陛下不委任天下賢俊，猥信此輩以為耳目，臣竊不取。」

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong sent Wude soldiers to secretly investigate distant-region affairs; Sizong shackled and sent them to the capital, then memorialized, saying, "Your Majesty does not entrust the worthy and talented throughout the realm, but rashly trusts men like these as eyes and ears—I respectfully cannot approve."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had sent Wude soldiers to secretly investigate affairs in distant regions. Sizong had them shackled and sent to the capital, then memorialized: "Your Majesty does not entrust affairs to the worthy and talented throughout the realm, but rashly trusts men like these as your eyes and ears—I respectfully cannot approve."

sentences.zh: 太宗怒其橫，遣使械嗣宗下吏，削秩。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong, angered by his insolence, sent emissaries to shackle Sizong and turn him over to the authorities, and reduced his rank.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong, angered by his insolence, sent emissaries to shackle Sizong and turn him over to the authorities, and reduced his rank.

sentences.zh: 會赦，復官，尋以秘書丞通判澶州，並河東西，植樹萬株，以固堤防。

translations.literal: An amnesty followed; he was restored to office. Soon he served as Secretariat Director and Vice Prefect of Chan Prefecture; along both banks of the Yellow River he planted ten thousand trees to strengthen the dikes.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty followed, and he was restored to office. Soon afterward he served as Secretariat Director and Vice Prefect of Chan Prefecture. Along both banks of the Yellow River he planted ten thousand trees to strengthen the dikes.

sentences.zh: 上言：「本州榷酤斗量，校以省斗不及七升，民犯私釀者三石以上坐死，有傷深峻，臣恐諸道率如此制，望詔自今並準省斗定罪。」

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial: "In this prefecture the monopoly liquor measure, compared with the standard provincial measure, amounts to less than seven sheng. Private brewing of three shi or more is punishable by death—the penalty is excessively harsh. I fear every circuit will follow this same regulation. I hope Your Majesty will issue an edict that from now on all such cases be judged according to the standard provincial measure."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "In this prefecture the monopoly liquor measure, compared with the standard provincial measure, amounts to less than seven sheng. Private brewing of three shi or more is punishable by death—the penalty is excessively harsh. I fear every circuit will follow this same regulation. I hope Your Majesty will issue an edict that from now on all such cases be judged according to the standard provincial measure."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 入為三司開拆推官，以左正言充河北轉運副使。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as an investigating officer in the Three Offices Bureaus' Opening and Inspection Division, and served as Left Reminder-in-Attendance and Deputy Commissioner of the Hebei Transportation Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as an investigating officer in the Three Offices Bureaus' Opening and Inspection Division, and served as Left Reminder-in-Attendance and Deputy Commissioner of the Hebei Transportation Circuit.

sentences.zh: 時邊境用兵，崔翰為大將，嗣宗每以苦言激其展效，就賜緋魚。

translations.literal: At the time the frontier was at war; Cui Han was the commanding general. Sizong repeatedly used stern words to spur him to distinction, and was promptly rewarded with the scarlet fish pouch.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the frontier was at war and Cui Han was the commanding general. Sizong repeatedly goaded him with stern words to spur him to distinction in battle, and was promptly rewarded with the scarlet fish pouch.

sentences.zh: 太宗將議親征，嗣宗上疏言契丹必不至之狀，甚見嘉納。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong was about to discuss a personal campaign, Sizong submitted a memorial stating the condition that the Khitans would certainly not come; it was greatly praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong was about to discuss a personal campaign, Sizong submitted a memorial arguing that the Khitans would certainly not come—a view that was highly praised and accepted.

sentences.zh: 改左司諫，賜白金千兩。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Left Reminder in the Department of State Affairs and granted a thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Left Reminder in the Department of State Affairs and granted a thousand taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 入為度支判官，改駕部員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as a fiscal management case officer and was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Chariots and Horses.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as a fiscal management case officer and was promoted to Vice Director of the Bureau of Chariots and Horses.

sentences.zh: 妻病，夜抉本司署門取藥，為直官宋鎬所發，坐罷職。

translations.literal: When his wife fell ill, he broke open the door of his bureau's office at night to obtain medicine; this was exposed by the duty officer Song Hao, and he was dismissed from office on that charge.
translations.idiomatic: When his wife fell ill, he broke open the door of his bureau's office at night to obtain medicine. The duty officer Song Hao exposed the act, and Sizong was dismissed from office on that charge.

sentences.zh: 頃之，出知興元府，徙京西轉運使。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent out as Prefect of Xingyuan and then transferred to Commissioner of the Jingxi Transportation Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out as Prefect of Xingyuan and then transferred to Commissioner of the Jingxi Transportation Circuit.

sentences.zh: 又移河北，賜金紫，貝州驍捷卒五十餘人謀竊發，嗣宗率吏悉擒之，優詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Hebei and granted the gold-and-purple insignia. More than fifty Xiaojie soldiers of Bei Prefecture plotted a surprise attack; Sizong led his officers and captured them all, and a specially favorable edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Hebei and granted the gold-and-purple insignia. More than fifty daring Xiaojie soldiers of Bei Prefecture plotted a surprise attack; Sizong led his officers and captured them all, and a specially favorable edict commended him.

sentences.zh: 遷虞部郎中，賜錢百萬。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Government Monopoly and granted a million cash.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Government Monopoly and granted a million cash.

sentences.zh: 至道初，移河東轉運使，以為政暴率聞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhidao reign he was transferred to Commissioner of the Hedong Transportation Circuit, becoming known for governing in a harsh and brusque manner.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhidao reign he was transferred to Commissioner of the Hedong Transportation Circuit, becoming known for governing in a harsh and brusque manner.

sentences.zh: 徙知耀州，又知同州，加比部郎中、淮南轉運使、江浙荊湖發運使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as Prefect of Yao Prefecture, then Prefect of Tong Prefecture, elevated to Director of the Bureau of Review, Commissioner of the Huainan Transportation Circuit, and Commissioner of Grain Transport for Jiangsu-Zhejiang and Jinghu.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as Prefect of Yao Prefecture, then Prefect of Tong Prefecture, elevated to Director of the Bureau of Review, Commissioner of the Huainan Transportation Circuit, and Commissioner of Grain Transport for Jiangsu-Zhejiang and Jinghu.

sentences.zh: 揚、楚間有窄家神廟，民有疾不餌藥，但竭致祀以徼福。

translations.literal: Between Yang and Chu there was a Zhai-family spirit temple. When people fell ill they would take no medicine but exhaust their resources in worship to beg for fortune.
translations.idiomatic: Between Yang and Chu there was a Zhai-family spirit temple. When people fell ill they took no medicine but exhausted their resources in worship to beg for fortune.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗撤其廟，選名方，刻石州門，自是民風稍變。

translations.literal: Sizong demolished the temple, selected renowned medical formulas, and had them carved on stone at the prefectural gate; from then on local custom gradually changed.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong demolished the temple, selected renowned medical formulas, and had them carved on stone at the prefectural gate; from then on local custom gradually changed.

sentences.zh: 初，漕運經泗州浮橋，舟多覆壞，嗣宗徙置城隅，遂獲安濟。

translations.literal: Earlier, grain transport had passed over Si Prefecture's floating bridge, and many boats capsized and were wrecked. Sizong had it relocated to a corner of the city wall, and safe passage was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, grain transport had passed over Si Prefecture's floating bridge, and many boats capsized and were wrecked. Sizong had it relocated to a corner of the city wall, and safe passage was achieved.

sentences.zh: 又建議外任官奉薄，貪猥者或致豐給，廉謹者終嬰貧匱，請以公田均賜之。

translations.literal: He also proposed that officials serving outside the capital receive thin salaries—the corrupt might still procure ample provision, while the upright and careful might end in poverty and want—and requested that public fields be divided and granted to them equally.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed that officials serving outside the capital receive thin salaries: the corrupt might still procure ample provision, while the upright and careful might end in poverty and want. He requested that public fields be divided and granted to them equally.

sentences.zh: 就改職方郎中。

translations.literal: He was then promoted to Director of the Bureau of Personnel Evaluations.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Director of the Bureau of Personnel Evaluations.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，以漕運稱職，就拜太常少卿。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping, for distinguished service in grain transport he was immediately appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping, for distinguished service in grain transport he was immediately appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以右諫議大夫充三司戶部使，改鹽鐵使。

translations.literal: The following year he served as Right Reminder-in-Waiting and Commissioner of the Three Offices Household Bureau, then was transferred to Salt and Iron Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he served as Right Reminder-in-Waiting and Commissioner of the Three Offices Household Bureau, then was transferred to Salt and Iron Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘗與度支使梁鼎、戶部使梁顥同對，言曰：「國家經費甚繁，賦入漸少，加以冗食者眾，尤為耗蠹，所宜裁節。

translations.literal: Once, together with Fiscal Commissioner Liang Ding and Household Commissioner Liang Hao, he had an audience and said, "State expenditures are very heavy and tax revenues are gradually shrinking. Added to this, the number of supernumeraries is large and especially drains resources—this ought to be cut back.
translations.idiomatic: Once, together with Fiscal Commissioner Liang Ding and Household Commissioner Liang Hao, he had an audience and said: "State expenditures are very heavy and tax revenues are gradually shrinking. Added to this, the number of supernumeraries is large and especially drains resources—this ought to be cut back.

sentences.zh: 若用度不足，即復重擾於民矣。

translations.literal: If expenditures are insufficient, the people will again be heavily burdened.
translations.idiomatic: If expenditures are insufficient, the people will again be heavily burdened.

sentences.zh: 況西北二邊未平，有饋運之煩，臣等會議，事可省者，願條列以聞。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the northwestern and northern frontiers are not yet pacified and there is the trouble of supply transport. We have met in conference and wish to submit an itemized list of matters that can be economized."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the northwestern and northern frontiers are not yet pacified and there is the trouble of supply transport. We have met in conference and wish to submit an itemized list of matters that can be economized."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 明年，將郊祀，嗣宗因條上應奉諸物以及工作，凡減雜物十萬六千，省工九萬九千。

translations.literal: The next year, as preparations were underway for the suburban sacrifice, Sizong submitted an itemized list of tribute items and labor projects, reducing miscellaneous goods by 106,000 and labor by 99,000.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, as preparations were underway for the suburban sacrifice, Sizong submitted an itemized list of tribute items and labor projects, reducing miscellaneous goods by 106,000 and labor by 99,000.

sentences.zh: 又言計省條奏，事有可紀者，望令判使一員，撰錄送史館。

translations.literal: He also said that among the fiscal department's submitted items there were matters worth recording, and requested that one supervising commissioner be assigned to compile and send them to the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed that among the fiscal department's memorial items, matters worth recording should be compiled by one supervising commissioner and sent to the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 詔以三司務繁，不當日有纂錄，可逐季錄送。

translations.literal: An edict responded that the Three Offices' business was heavy and daily compilation was inappropriate; records could be submitted quarterly.
translations.idiomatic: An edict responded that the Three Offices' business was heavy and daily compilation was inappropriate; records could be submitted quarterly.

sentences.zh: 會罷三部使，改左諫議大夫，知通進、銀臺司兼門下封駁事，出知幷州兼幷代部署。

translations.literal: When the three commissionerships were abolished, he was made Left Reminder-in-Waiting, put in charge of the Memorial Reception and Silver Terrace Office with concurrent duty for seal-and-return review in the Chancellery, and sent out as Prefect of Bing Prefecture with concurrent command of the Bing-Dai garrison command.
translations.idiomatic: When the three commissionerships were abolished, he was made Left Reminder-in-Waiting, put in charge of the Memorial Reception and Silver Terrace Office with concurrent duty for seal-and-return review in the Chancellery, and sent out as Prefect of Bing Prefecture with concurrent command of the Bing-Dai garrison command.

sentences.zh: 州境有臥龍王廟，每窮冬，闔境致祭，值風雪寒甚，老幼踣於道，嗣宗亟毀之。

translations.literal: Within the prefecture was a Sleeping Dragon King temple. Every deep winter the whole territory would turn out for sacrifice; caught in fierce wind and snow, old and young collapsed in the roads. Sizong promptly destroyed it.
translations.idiomatic: Within the prefecture was a Sleeping Dragon King temple. Every deep winter the whole territory would turn out for sacrifice; caught in fierce wind and snow, old and young collapsed in the roads. Sizong promptly destroyed it.

sentences.zh: 轉運使鄭文寶上其政績，有詔褒美。

translations.literal: Transportation Commissioner Zheng Wenbao submitted a report on his administrative achievements, and an edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Transportation Commissioner Zheng Wenbao submitted a report on his administrative achievements, and an edict praised him.

sentences.zh: 先是，西邊市馬，以給北邊戰士，有瘠弱者即送闕下，暑月道遠多死。

translations.literal: Previously, horses were purchased on the western frontier to supply northern border troops. Weak and emaciated ones were sent to the capital; in the heat of summer the long journey killed many.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, horses were purchased on the western frontier to supply northern border troops. Weak and emaciated ones were sent to the capital; in the heat of summer the long journey killed many.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗建議，以汾州地涼，接樓煩諸監，美水草，請就牧放，從之。

translations.literal: Sizong proposed that since Fen Prefecture had a cool climate and bordered the Loufan horse pastures with fine grass and water, the horses should be grazed there instead. The proposal was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong proposed that since Fen Prefecture had a cool climate and bordered the Loufan horse pastures with fine grass and water, the horses should be grazed there instead. The proposal was accepted.

sentences.zh: 召拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符間，真宗告謁太廟，嗣宗立班失儀，因自首。

translations.literal: During the Dazhong Xiangfu era, when Emperor Zhenzong performed rites at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Sizong breached protocol in the formation and confessed.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong Xiangfu era, when Emperor Zhenzong performed rites at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Sizong breached protocol in the formation and confessed.

sentences.zh: 真宗謂憲官當守禮法，以其性粗略，不之責。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong said that a censor ought to observe ritual and law, but given his rough and careless nature, did not hold him accountable.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong said that a censor ought to observe ritual and law, but given his rough and careless nature, did not hold him accountable.

sentences.zh: 加兼工部侍郎、權判吏部銓。

translations.literal: He was additionally appointed Vice Minister of Works and given provisional charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection board.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Vice Minister of Works and given provisional charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection board.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗剛果率易，無所畏憚，每進見，極談時事，或及人間細務。

translations.literal: Sizong was firm, resolute, and blunt, afraid of nothing. At every audience he spoke at length on current affairs, sometimes even touching on petty matters among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong was firm, resolute, and blunt, afraid of nothing. At every audience he spoke at length on current affairs, sometimes even touching on petty matters among the people.

sentences.zh: 頗輕險好進，深詆參知政事馮拯之短，遂結宰相王旦弟旭，使達意於旦以為助。

translations.literal: He was rather reckless and ambitious, bitterly assailing Vice Grand Councilor Feng Zheng's faults, and cultivated alliance with Grand Councilor Wang Dan's younger brother Xu, having him convey his wishes to Dan for support.
translations.idiomatic: He was rather reckless and ambitious, bitterly assailing Vice Grand Councilor Feng Zheng's faults, and cultivated alliance with Grand Councilor Wang Dan's younger brother Xu, having him convey his wishes to Dan for support.

sentences.zh: 旦疾其醜行，因力庇拯，嗣宗大怒。

translations.literal: Dan detested his vile conduct and therefore vigorously shielded Feng Zheng. Sizong was furious.
translations.idiomatic: Dan detested his vile conduct and therefore vigorously shielded Feng Zheng. Sizong was furious.

sentences.zh: 知制誥王曾從妹適孔冕家，閨門不睦。

translations.literal: Executive Drafting Academician Wang Zeng's younger female cousin by marriage had married into Kong Mian's family, and relations within the household were strained.
translations.idiomatic: Executive Drafting Academician Wang Zeng's younger female cousin by marriage had married into Kong Mian's family, and relations within the household were strained.

sentences.zh: 曾從東封，至冕家啜茗中毒，得良藥乃解。

translations.literal: When Zeng was returning from the eastern tour of the sacred Mount Tai, he stopped at Mian's home to drink tea and was poisoned; only after obtaining effective medicine was he saved.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng was returning from the eastern tour of the sacred Mount Tai, he stopped at Mian's home to drink tea and was poisoned; only after obtaining effective medicine was he saved.

sentences.zh: 事已暴露，曾密疏方行大禮，願罷推究。

translations.literal: The matter had already come to light. Zeng sent a secret memorial that the grand rites were about to be performed and asked that investigation be halted.
translations.idiomatic: The matter had already come to light. Zeng sent a secret memorial that the grand rites were about to be performed and asked that investigation be halted.

sentences.zh: 宰相亦以冕先聖後，將有褒擢，乃隱其事。

translations.literal: The grand councilors also considered that Mian was a descendant of the Sage and was slated for promotion, and therefore concealed the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The grand councilors also considered that Mian was a descendant of the Sage and was slated for promotion, and therefore concealed the affair.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗獨謂曾誣構冕，懼反坐，乃求寢息。

translations.literal: Sizong alone held that Zeng had framed Mian. Fearful of being counter-charged, he asked that the matter be laid to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong alone held that Zeng had framed Mian. Fearful of being counter-charged, he asked that the matter be laid to rest.

sentences.zh: 會愆雨，嗣宗請對，言：「孔冕為王曾所訟，儻朝旨鞫問，加之鍛煉，則冕終負冤枉。

translations.literal: When drought persisted, Sizong requested an audience and said, "Kong Mian was accused by Wang Zeng. If an imperial order should interrogate him and torture is applied to extract confession, Mian will finally bear a false charge.
translations.idiomatic: When drought persisted, Sizong requested an audience and said: "Kong Mian was accused by Wang Zeng. If an imperial order should interrogate him and torture is applied to extract confession, Mian will finally bear a false charge.

sentences.zh: 又侯德昭援赦敘緋，年考未滿，以欺詐得之，非吏部令史自首，亦無由知。

translations.literal: Furthermore, Hou Dezhao obtained scarlet rank by invoking amnesty restitution, though his years of evaluation were incomplete—he secured it by fraud. Had not a Ministry of Personnel clerk confessed, there would have been no way to know.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, Hou Dezhao obtained scarlet rank by invoking amnesty restitution, though his years of evaluation were incomplete—he secured it by fraud. Had not a Ministry of Personnel clerk confessed, there would have been no way to know.

sentences.zh: 沿堂行首李永錫坐贓除名，復引充舊職，尋送銓授令錄。」

translations.literal: Hall-line chief Li Yongxi was dismissed and struck from the rolls for corruption, yet was recalled to his former post and soon sent to the selection board for appointment as a county recorder."
translations.idiomatic: Hall-line chief Li Yongxi was dismissed and struck from the rolls for corruption, yet was recalled to his former post and soon sent to the selection board for appointment as a county recorder."

sentences.zh: 真宗亟召王旦等詰之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong promptly summoned Wang Dan and the others to question them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong promptly summoned Wang Dan and the others to question them.

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「孔冕之罪，朝議特為容隱，不令按問，誠非冤枉也。

translations.literal: Wang Dan said, "Kong Mian's guilt was deliberately concealed by court deliberation—we simply forbade investigation. He is truly not wrongfully charged.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan said: "Kong Mian's guilt was deliberately concealed by court deliberation—we simply forbade investigation. He is truly not wrongfully charged.

sentences.zh: 德昭據吏部奏驗，乃行制命，及其首露，即已追奪。

translations.literal: Dezhao's appointment was issued on the basis of Ministry verification; once he was exposed, the appointment was immediately revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao's appointment was issued on the basis of Ministry verification; once he was exposed, the appointment was immediately revoked.

sentences.zh: 永錫先為縣吏，坐為本部節度市羊不輸算除名，及沿堂闕人，李沆以其魁梧，因選擬官，復用為副行首。

translations.literal: Yongxi had formerly been a county clerk, dismissed for purchasing sheep for the circuit military commissioner without paying the excise. When the hall line was short of men, Li Hang selected him for his imposing stature and restored him as deputy line chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi had formerly been a county clerk, dismissed for purchasing sheep for the circuit military commissioner without paying the excise. When the hall line was short of men, Li Hang selected him for his imposing stature and restored him as deputy line chief.

sentences.zh: 在省祗事四年，陳牒乞班敘用，因復送銓。」

translations.literal: After four years of service in the ministry he submitted a petition requesting reappointment by seniority, and was sent back to the selection board."
translations.idiomatic: After four years of service in the ministry he submitted a petition requesting reappointment by seniority, and was sent back to the selection board."

sentences.zh: 真宗曰：「止此，乃致旱邪？」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong said, "Only these matters, and they caused the drought?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong said: "Only these matters, and they caused the drought?"

sentences.zh: 嗣宗理屈，復以他辭侵旦，旦不與抗，乃已。

translations.literal: Sizong, having lost the argument, again attacked Dan on other grounds; Dan did not engage him, and the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong, having lost the argument, again attacked Dan on other grounds; Dan did not engage him, and the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 明年十月，嗣宗復請對，言：「去歲八月至今年十月不雨，宿麥不登。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the following year Sizong again requested an audience, saying, "From the eighth month of last year until this tenth month there has been no rain; the winter wheat has failed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the following year Sizong again requested an audience, saying: "From the eighth month of last year until this tenth month there has been no rain; the winter wheat has failed.

sentences.zh: 及秋，兗、鄆苦雨，河溢害稼，刑政有失，致成災沴。

translations.literal: In autumn Yan and Yun suffered bitter rains; the river overflowed and ruined the crops. Failings in law and punishment have produced this calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn Yan and Yun suffered bitter rains; the river overflowed and ruined the crops. Failings in law and punishment have produced this calamity.

sentences.zh: 孔冕冤枉，播在人口，王曾尚居近班，願示黜退，以正朝典，臣請露章以聞。」

translations.literal: Kong Mian's wrongful conviction is on everyone's lips, yet Wang Zeng still holds a place near the throne. I ask that he be publicly demoted to set right court standards. I request leave to submit an open memorial on the matter."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Mian's wrongful conviction is on everyone's lips, yet Wang Zeng still holds a place near the throne. I ask that he be publicly demoted to set right court standards. I request leave to submit an open memorial on the matter."

sentences.zh: 真宗語王旦等曰：「曾實無罪，若嗣宗上章，亦須裁處。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong told Wang Dan and the others, "Zeng is in fact innocent. Even if Sizong submits his memorial, it too must be adjudicated."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong told Wang Dan and the others: "Zeng is in fact innocent. Even if Sizong submits his memorial, it too must be adjudicated."

sentences.zh: 旦曰：「冕不善之跡甚眾，但以宣聖之後不欲窮究，謂其冤枉，感傷和氣，恐未近理。」

translations.literal: Wang Dan said, "Mian's misdeeds are many, but because he is a descendant of the Sage we did not wish to pursue the matter thoroughly. To call him wrongfully charged and say harmony has been harmed—perhaps that is not quite reasonable."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan said: "Mian's misdeeds are many, but because he is a descendant of the Sage we did not wish to pursue the matter thoroughly. To call him wrongfully charged and say harmony has been harmed—perhaps that is not quite reasonable."

sentences.zh: 趙安仁曰：「今若再行按問，冕何能免罪？」

translations.literal: Zhao Anren said, "If we investigate again now, how could Mian escape guilt?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Anren said: "If we investigate again now, how could Mian escape guilt?"

sentences.zh: 王欽若曰：「臣請審問嗣宗，若再鞫冕，不能自隱，如何區處？」

translations.literal: Wang Qinruo said, "I ask to interrogate Sizong: if Mian is tried again and the truth cannot be concealed, how shall we dispose of the matter?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo said: "I ask to interrogate Sizong: if Mian is tried again and the truth cannot be concealed, how shall we dispose of the matter?"

sentences.zh: 明日，嗣宗復對，且謝前言之失，真宗亦優容之。

translations.literal: The next day Sizong had another audience and apologized for his earlier errors; Emperor Zhenzong was lenient with him as well.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Sizong had another audience and apologized for his earlier errors; Emperor Zhenzong was lenient with him as well.

sentences.zh: 其強妄多此類。

translations.literal: His arrogance and presumption were often of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His arrogance and presumption were often of this sort.

sentences.zh: 將祀汾陰，以永興重地，思得大臣才兼文武者鎮之。

translations.literal: When preparations were underway for the sacrifice at Fen-yin, since Yongxing was a strategically vital region the emperor sought a senior minister versed in both civil and military affairs to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: When preparations were underway for the sacrifice at Fen-yin, since Yongxing was a strategically vital region the emperor sought a senior minister versed in both civil and military affairs to guard it.

sentences.zh: 因謂宰相曰：「嗣宗嘗自言知武事，可授廉車以當此任，宜召問之。」

translations.literal: He therefore told the grand councilors, "Sizong has said of himself that he understands military affairs. He could be given a surveillance commissionership for this post—I should summon and ask him."
translations.idiomatic: He therefore told the grand councilors: "Sizong has said of himself that he understands military affairs. He could be given a surveillance commissionership for this post—I should summon and ask him."

sentences.zh: 嗣宗願奉詔，即拜耀州觀察使、知永興軍府。

translations.literal: Sizong declared himself willing to obey the summons and was immediately appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Yao Prefecture and Military Prefect of Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong declared himself willing to obey the summons and was immediately appointed Surveillance Commissioner of Yao Prefecture and Military Prefect of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 真宗作詩賜之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong composed a poem and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong composed a poem and bestowed it on him.

sentences.zh: 時种放得告歸山，嗣宗逆於傳舍，禮之甚厚。

translations.literal: At the time Zhong Fang had obtained leave to return to the mountains. Sizong received him at the relay station and treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhong Fang had obtained leave to return to the mountains. Sizong received him at the relay station and treated him with great courtesy.

sentences.zh: 放既醉，稍倨，嗣宗怒，以語譏放。

translations.literal: Once Fang was drunk he grew somewhat arrogant; Sizong grew angry and used words to mock him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Fang was drunk he grew somewhat arrogant; Sizong grew angry and used words to mock him.

sentences.zh: 放曰：「君以手搏得狀元耳，何足道也！」

translations.literal: Fang said, "You won first place by grappling with your hands—what is there to boast of!"
translations.idiomatic: Fang said: "You won first place by grappling with your hands—what is there to boast of!"

sentences.zh: 初，嗣宗就試講武殿，搏趙昌言帽，擢首科，故放及之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sizong took the military examination in the Hall of Martial Lectures, he seized Zhao Changyan's hat in a wrestling bout and was placed first in the examination—hence Fang's jibe.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Sizong took the military examination in the Hall of Martial Lectures, he seized Zhao Changyan's hat in a wrestling bout and was placed first in the examination—hence Fang's jibe.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗愧恨，因上疏言：「所部兼並之家，侵漁眾民，淩暴孤寡，凡十餘族，而放為之首。

translations.literal: Humiliated and resentful, Sizong submitted a memorial saying, "Within my jurisdiction there are more than ten powerful land-grabbing clans that encroach on the people and bully the orphaned and widowed—and Fang is their ringleader.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated and resentful, Sizong submitted a memorial saying: "Within my jurisdiction there are more than ten powerful land-grabbing clans that encroach on the people and bully the orphaned and widowed—and Fang is their ringleader.

sentences.zh: 放弟侄無賴，據林麓樵采，周回二百餘里，奪編厚利。

translations.literal: Fang's younger brothers and nephews are ruffians who monopolize forestry and firewood gathering across more than two hundred li, seizing substantial profits.
translations.idiomatic: Fang's younger brothers and nephews are ruffians who monopolize forestry and firewood gathering across more than two hundred li, seizing substantial profits.

sentences.zh: 願以臣疏下放，賜放終南田百畝，徙放嵩山。」

translations.literal: I ask that my memorial be forwarded to demote Fang, grant him a hundred mu of fields on Mount Zhongnan, and relocate him to Mount Song."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that my memorial be forwarded to demote Fang, grant him a hundred mu of fields on Mount Zhongnan, and relocate him to Mount Song."

sentences.zh: 疏辭極於詬辱，至目放為魑魅。

translations.literal: The memorial's language was wildly abusive, going so far as to call Fang a demon.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial's language was wildly abusive, going so far as to call Fang a demon.

sentences.zh: 真宗方厚待放，令徙居嵩陽避之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong, who was still treating Fang with favor, ordered him to move to Songyang to avoid Sizong.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong, who was still treating Fang with favor, ordered him to move to Songyang to avoid Sizong.

sentences.zh: 四年，邠寧陳興擅釋劫盜，徙嗣宗知邠州兼邠寧環慶路都部署。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Chen Xing of Binning arbitrarily released robbers; Sizong was transferred to Prefect of Bin Prefecture with concurrent command of the Binning-Huanqing Circuit garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Chen Xing of Binning arbitrarily released robbers; Sizong was transferred to Prefect of Bin Prefecture with concurrent command of the Binning-Huanqing Circuit garrison.

sentences.zh: 城東有靈應公廟，傍有山穴，群狐處焉，妖巫挾之為人禍福，民甚信向，水旱疾疫悉禱之，民語為之諱「狐」音。

translations.literal: East of the city was a Spirit-Responding Duke temple. Beside it was a mountain cave where a pack of foxes dwelled; sorcerers exploited them to bring people weal or woe. The people believed fervently and prayed there for rain, drought, disease, and plague alike; in speech they even tabooed the sound for "fox."
translations.idiomatic: East of the city was a Spirit-Responding Duke temple. Beside it was a mountain cave where a pack of foxes dwelled; sorcerers exploited them to bring people weal or woe. The people believed fervently and prayed there for rain, drought, disease, and plague alike; in speech they even tabooed the sound for "fox."

sentences.zh: 前此長吏，皆先謁廟然後視事。

translations.literal: Previous magistrates had all paid homage at the temple before taking up their duties.
translations.idiomatic: Previous magistrates had all paid homage at the temple before taking up their duties.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗毀其廟，熏其穴，得數十狐，盡殺之，淫祀遂息。

translations.literal: Sizong destroyed the temple, smoked out the cave, took several dozen foxes, and killed them all; the illicit cult ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong destroyed the temple, smoked out the cave, took several dozen foxes, and killed them all; the illicit cult ceased.

sentences.zh: 徙知鎮州，發邊肅姦贓，肅坐貶。

translations.literal: Transferred to Prefect of Zhen Prefecture, he exposed Bian Su's corruption; Bian was demoted on that charge.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Prefect of Zhen Prefecture, he exposed Bian Su's corruption; Bian was demoted on that charge.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗嘗言徙种放、掘邠狐、按邊肅，為去三害。

translations.literal: Sizong once said that exiling Zhong Fang, digging out the Bin foxes, and prosecuting Bian Su were removing three scourges.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong once said that exiling Zhong Fang, digging out the Bin foxes, and prosecuting Bian Su were removing three scourges.

sentences.zh: 居二歲，召還，授樞密副使、檢校太保。

translations.literal: After two years he was recalled and appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs with the honorary title of Grand Protector.
translations.idiomatic: After two years he was recalled and appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs with the honorary title of Grand Protector.

sentences.zh: 寇準為使，嗣宗與之不叶，累表解職，授檢校太傅、大同軍節度、知許州。

translations.literal: Kou Zhun was commissioner; Sizong did not get along with him and repeatedly submitted memorials resigning, and was appointed Honorary Grand Mentor, Military Governor of Datong Army, and Prefect of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun was commissioner; Sizong did not get along with him and repeatedly submitted memorials resigning, and was appointed Honorary Grand Mentor, Military Governor of Datong Army, and Prefect of Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗嘗遊是州，別墅在焉，時人以為榮。

translations.literal: Sizong had once traveled in that prefecture and had a villa there; people of the time regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong had once traveled in that prefecture and had a villa there; people of the time regarded it as an honor.

sentences.zh: 移知河南府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Henan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Prefect of Henan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天禧初，改感德軍節度，洛下訛言相驚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianxi he was changed to Military Governor of Gande Army; false rumors in Luoyang alarmed the populace.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianxi he was changed to Military Governor of Gande Army; false rumors in Luoyang alarmed the populace.

sentences.zh: 徙知陝州，再表請老，且求入覲，遣使召還。

translations.literal: Transferred to Prefect of Shan Prefecture, he twice memorialized requesting retirement and also asked to come to court; emissaries were sent to summon him back.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Prefect of Shan Prefecture, he twice memorialized requesting retirement and also asked to come to court; emissaries were sent to summon him back.

sentences.zh: 郊祀，改靜難軍節度。

translations.literal: At the suburban sacrifice he was made Military Governor of Jingnan Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban sacrifice he was made Military Governor of Jingnan Army.

sentences.zh: 既至闕下，病足，不能朝謁，乃求再知許州，不復議休退。

translations.literal: Once he reached the capital his feet were afflicted and he could not attend court audience, so he asked to be Prefect of Xu Prefecture again and no longer pressed for retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the capital his feet were afflicted and he could not attend court audience, so he asked to be Prefect of Xu Prefecture again and no longer pressed for retirement.

sentences.zh: 寇準為相，素惡之，特命以左屯衛上將軍、檢校太尉致仕。

translations.literal: Kou Zhun was grand councilor and had long disliked him; he was specially ordered to retire as General-in-Chief of the Left Palace Guard and Honorary Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun was grand councilor and had long disliked him; he was specially ordered to retire as General-in-Chief of the Left Palace Guard and Honorary Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 表求面辭，以足疾艱於拜起，特免舞蹈，許其子扶掖之。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting a personal farewell audience; because his foot ailment made bowing difficult, he was specially exempted from the full prostration ritual and permitted to be supported by his son.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial requesting a personal farewell audience; because his foot ailment made bowing difficult, he was specially exempted from the full prostration ritual and permitted to be supported by his son.

sentences.zh: 對數刻，賜錢百萬，還許下。

translations.literal: After an audience of several quarters of an hour he was granted a million cash and returned to Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After an audience of several quarters of an hour he was granted a million cash and returned to Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 準貶，朝議以嗣宗藩輔舊臣，特令月給奉五十千。

translations.literal: When Kou was demoted, court deliberation held that Sizong, as a former frontier-supporting senior minister, should be specially granted a monthly stipend of fifty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: When Kou was demoted, court deliberation held that Sizong, as a former frontier-supporting senior minister, should be specially granted a monthly stipend of fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗尤睦宗族，撫諸侄如己子，著遺戒以訓子孫勿得析居，又令以《孝經》、弓劍、筆硯置壙中。

translations.literal: Sizong was especially harmonious with the clan group, raising all his nephews like his own sons; he wrote testamentary injunctions instructing descendants not to divide households, and also ordered the Classic of Filial Piety, bow and sword, brush and inkstone placed in the tomb chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong was devoted to his kin, treating his nephews as if they were his own sons; he left testamentary instructions forbidding descendants to live apart, and directed that the Classic of Filial Piety, a bow and sword, and writing brush and inkstone be buried with him.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died, age seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the reign he died at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 廢朝，贈侍中。

translations.literal: Court audience was suspended; he was posthumously made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning was declared, and he was posthumously conferred the title of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 諡曰景莊。

translations.literal: The posthumous name was Jingzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Jingzhuang (Resplendent and Dignified).

sentences.zh: 錄其子二人、甥二人官。

translations.literal: His two sons and two nephews were recorded for office.
translations.idiomatic: Offices were granted to his two sons and two nephews.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗事三朝，最為宿舊。

translations.literal: Sizong served three reigns and was the most senior of the old retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong had served three emperors and ranked among the most venerable of the old guard.

sentences.zh: 所至以嚴明御下，尤傲狠，務以醜言淩挫群類。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he governed subordinates with severity and clarity, especially proud and harsh, striving to use ugly words to overwhelm and humiliate all sorts of people.
translations.idiomatic: In every post he ruled subordinates with stern discipline, but he was also notably arrogant and ruthless, habitually using abusive language to browbeat those around him.

sentences.zh: 為中丞日，嘗忿宋白、郭贄、邢昺七十不請老，屢請真宗敕其休致，又遣親屬諷激之。

translations.literal: When he was censor-in-chief, he was once angered that Song Bai, Guo Zhi, and Xing Bing at seventy did not request old-age retirement; he repeatedly asked Zhenzong to order their retirement from office, and also sent relatives to prod and goad them.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as censor-in-chief, he took offense that Song Bai, Guo Zhi, and Xing Bing had reached seventy yet refused to retire; he repeatedly petitioned Zhenzong to compel their withdrawal from office and even sent relatives to needle them into doing so.

sentences.zh: 及嗣宗晚歲疾甚，猶享厚祿，徘徊不去，嘗謂人曰：「僕惟此一事，未能免物議。」

translations.literal: When Sizong in his late years was gravely ill, he still enjoyed a generous salary and lingered without leaving; he once said to people: "I have only this one matter for which I cannot escape public criticism."
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Sizong himself grew seriously ill in old age, he continued to draw a lavish stipend and hesitated to step down; he once remarked to others, "This is the one thing for which I cannot escape censure."

sentences.zh: 眾皆嗤之。

translations.literal: All mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone scoffed at the hypocrisy.

sentences.zh: 嗣宗好為文，而劄尤甚。

translations.literal: Sizong liked to compose literature, and memorials especially so.
translations.idiomatic: Sizong was fond of writing, and memorials in particular.

sentences.zh: 奉祀之歲，近臣皆為頌記，宰相以嗣宗所撰，不足發揮盛德，慮為後所誚，乃不許刻石。

translations.literal: In the year of the state sacrifice, close ministers all wrote eulogies; the chief councilor thought Sizong's composition insufficient to unfold the grand virtue, fearing mockery from later generations, and therefore did not permit it carved on stone.
translations.idiomatic: During the year of the state sacrifice, the emperor's close ministers all composed commemorative essays; the chief councilor judged Sizong's piece too weak to do justice to the emperor's greatness and, fearing posterity's ridicule, refused to allow it inscribed on stone.

sentences.zh: 所著有《中陵子》三十卷。

translations.literal: His writings included the Zhonglingzi in thirty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He authored the Zhonglingzi in thirty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 子堯臣，內殿承制；

translations.literal: His son Yao Chen, Inner Palace Commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: His son Yao Chen served as Inner Palace Commissioner;

sentences.zh: 唐臣，太子中舍；

translations.literal: Tang Chen, Vice Director in the Crown Prince's Household;
translations.idiomatic: Tang Chen held the post of Vice Director in the Crown Prince's Household;

sentences.zh: 從子舜臣，供奉官、閤門祗候；
