translations.literal: His nephew Shun Chen, Attendant-in-Waiting and Gatekeeper Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Shun Chen served as Attendant-in-Waiting and Gatekeeper Attendant;

sentences.zh: 禹臣，太子中舍。

translations.literal: Yu Chen, Vice Director in the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chen held the post of Vice Director in the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 李昌齡

translations.literal: Li Changling
translations.idiomatic: The biography continues with Li Changling.

sentences.zh: 李昌齡，字天錫，宋州楚丘人。

translations.literal: Li Changling, style name Tianxi, a man of Chuqiu in Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changling, courtesy name Tianxi, was a native of Chuqiu in Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曾祖確，膠水令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Que was magistrate of Jiaoshui.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Que had served as magistrate of Jiaoshui.

sentences.zh: 祖譚，邯鄲令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Tan was magistrate of Handan.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Tan had been magistrate of Handan.

sentences.zh: 父運，太常卿。

translations.literal: His father Yun was Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yun rose to Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 昌齡，太平興國三年舉進士，大理評事、通判合州。

translations.literal: Changling passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Taiping Xingguo, became Assistant Evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review and judicial intendant of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Changling passed the jinshi examination in Taiping Xingguo 3 (978) and was appointed Assistant Evaluator in the Court of Judicial Review and judicial intendant of He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷將作監丞、右贊善大夫、通判銀州。

translations.literal: He successively served as Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, Right Viscount of Goodness in the Crown Prince's Household, and judicial intendant of Yin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He then held the posts of Vice Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, Right Viscount of Goodness in the Crown Prince's Household, and judicial intendant of Yin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 京城開金明池，昌齡獻詩百韻，太宗嘉之，擢右拾遺、直史館，賜緋。

translations.literal: When the capital opened Jinming Pool, Changling presented a hundred-rhyme poem; Taizong praised it and promoted him to Right Reminder, Direct Attachment to the Historiography Institute, granting red rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinming Pool was opened in the capital, Changling submitted a hundred-couplet poem that pleased Taizong, who promoted him to Right Reminder with direct attachment to the Historiography Institute and granted him red rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 改右補闕，出知滁州。

translations.literal: Changed to Right Supplementary Censor; sent out as prefect of Chu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Supplementary Censor and appointed prefect of Chu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，起為淮南轉運使，轉戶部員外郎、知廣州。

translations.literal: Upon mourning for his mother, he was recalled as Huainan Transport Commissioner, then transferred to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and prefect of Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the death of his mother he was recalled from mourning to serve as Huainan Transport Commissioner, then promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and appointed prefect of Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 廣有海舶之饒，昌齡不能以廉自守，淳化二年代還。

translations.literal: Guang had the riches of ocean-going merchant ships; Changling could not keep himself with integrity; in the second year of Chunhua he was replaced and recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Guang Prefecture's maritime trade brought great wealth, but Changling failed to remain honest; he was recalled and replaced in Chunhua 2 (991).

sentences.zh: 初，運嘗典許州，有第在城中，昌齡包苴輜重悉留貯焉，其至京城，但藥物藥器而已。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yun had once administered Xu Prefecture and had a mansion in the city; Changling left all wrapped gifts and heavy baggage stored there; when he reached the capital, only medicines and medical implements.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier his father Yun had served as prefect of Xu and owned a residence in the city; Changling stored all his bribe-laden baggage there, bringing only medicines and medical instruments when he reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 會有言其貪者，太宗以為誣，召賜金紫，擢禮部郎中，逾月，為樞密直學士。

translations.literal: When someone spoke of his greed, Taizong thought it slander, summoned and granted gold and purple insignia, promoted to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites; after a month, made Privy Council Academic Scholar.
translations.idiomatic: When accusations of corruption reached the throne, Taizong dismissed them as slander, summoned Changling, granted him gold and purple insignia, and promoted him to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Rites; within a month he was made Privy Council Academic Scholar.

sentences.zh: 昌齡上言：「廣州市舶，每歲商舶至，官盡增價買之，良苦相雜，少利。

translations.literal: Changling submitted a memorial: "Guang Prefecture's maritime trade office—each year when merchant ships arrive, the government buys everything at marked-up prices; good and bad are mixed together, with little profit.
translations.idiomatic: Changling memorialized: "At Guang Prefecture's maritime trade office, whenever merchant vessels arrive the government buys the entire cargo at inflated prices, mixing fine goods with shoddy ones to little profit.

sentences.zh: 自今請擇其良者，官如價給之，苦者恣其賣，勿禁。

translations.literal: From now on please select the good ones; let the government pay market price; let the poor ones be sold freely without prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the government should purchase only the best goods at fair market prices and allow inferior merchandise to be sold freely without restriction.

sentences.zh: 雷、化、新、白、惠、恩等州山林有群象，民能取其牙，官禁不得賣。

translations.literal: In Lei, Hua, Xin, Bai, Hui, En and other prefectures' mountains and forests there are herds of elephants; the people can obtain their tusks, but official prohibition forbids selling them.
translations.idiomatic: In the mountain forests of Lei, Hua, Xin, Bai, Hui, En, and other prefectures wild elephants roam; though locals can harvest ivory, the government currently forbids its sale.

sentences.zh: 自今宜令送官，以半價償之，有敢隱匿及私市與人者，論如法。」

translations.literal: From now on it should be ordered sent to the government, compensated at half price; those who dare conceal or privately sell to others should be punished according to law."
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter ivory should be delivered to the government for half-price compensation, and anyone who conceals it or sells it privately should be prosecuted under the statutes."

sentences.zh: 詔皆從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 是秋，初置審刑院於禁中。

translations.literal: That autumn, the Office for the Review of Punishments was first established inside the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Office for the Review of Punishments was first established within the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 凡獄具上奏，先申審刑院，印付大理、刑部斷覆以聞，又下審刑中覆裁決，以付中書，當者行之，否則宰相聞以論決。

translations.literal: Whenever case documents were submitted, they were first reported to the Office for the Review of Punishments, sealed and sent to the Court of Judicial Review and Ministry of Justice for judgment and review to be reported; then sent down to the Review Office for re-review and decision, delivered to the Secretariat; if correct they were carried out, otherwise the chief councilor was informed for deliberation and decision.
translations.idiomatic: All submitted case files were first routed through the Office for the Review of Punishments, then forwarded with an official seal to the Court of Judicial Review and Ministry of Justice for initial judgment and review; the case then returned to the Review Office for a second ruling before being sent to the Secretariat-Chancellery for execution, or, if disputed, referred to the chief councilor for final adjudication.

sentences.zh: 命昌齡知院事。

translations.literal: Changling was ordered to administer the office affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Changling was appointed to head the new office.

sentences.zh: 月餘，又權判吏部流內銓，數日，授右諫議大夫，充戶部使。

translations.literal: After a little over a month, he was also given temporary charge of the Ministry of Personnel's Registry of Current Appointments; after several days, granted Right Remonstrance Grandee and made Commissioner of the Households Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was also given temporary charge of the Ministry of Personnel's registry of current appointments; within days he was made Right Remonstrance Grandee and Commissioner of the Households Bureau.

sentences.zh: 三年，改度支使，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the third year, changed to Commissioner of the Revenue Bureau, invested as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Commissioner of the Revenue Bureau and appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 下詔御史臺，合行故事並條奏以聞，獄無大小，自中丞以下皆親臨鞫問，不得專責所司，李繼隆受命河朔征討，不赴臺辭，昌齡糾之，遣吏追還，罰奉。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to the Censorate directing that established precedents be itemized and reported; cases great and small, from the censor-in-chief downward, were all to conduct interrogation in person and not delegate exclusively to subordinate offices. Li Jilong received orders for the Hebei campaign and did not come to the Censorate to take leave; Changling impeached him, sent officials to pursue and recall him, and fined his salary.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed the Censorate to itemize all established precedents for the throne's review and required that cases of every size be personally heard by the censor-in-chief and his subordinates rather than delegated to clerks. When Li Jilong, ordered north on campaign, failed to call at the Censorate to bid farewell, Changling impeached him, had officials sent to bring him back, and levied a fine on his salary.

sentences.zh: 又劾陝西轉運使鄭文寶生事邊境，築城沙磧，輕變禁法，文寶坐貶湖外。

translations.literal: He also impeached Shaanxi Transport Commissioner Zheng Wenbao for stirring up trouble on the frontier, building fortifications in sandy desert, lightly changing prohibition laws; Wenbao was demoted beyond the lakes.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Shaanxi Transport Commissioner Zheng Wenbao for provoking trouble on the frontier by building fortifications in the desert and rashly altering trade restrictions; Wenbao was demoted to a post beyond Dongting.

sentences.zh: 至道二年，以本官參知政事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhidao, with his existing office he became Participating Administrator of Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhidao 2 (996) he was promoted to Participating Administrator of Affairs while retaining his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 占謝便殿，太宗謂曰：「中書政本，當進用善良，博詢眾議，以正道臨之，即怨謗無由而生矣。」

translations.literal: At the audience of thanks in the Convenient Hall, Taizong said to him: "The Secretariat is the foundation of government; one should advance and employ the good and virtuous, broadly consult many opinions, and govern them with the correct Way—then complaints and slander will have no basis to arise."
translations.idiomatic: At his audience of thanks in the Convenient Hall, Taizong told him: "The Secretariat is the root of governance; you must promote worthy men, seek counsel widely, and lead by the proper path—then slander will find no foothold."

sentences.zh: 昌齡居位，頗選愞，無所建明。

translations.literal: Changling in office was quite weak and conforming, establishing nothing clear.
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, however, Changling proved timid and indecisive, advancing no significant policies.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，加戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong acceded, he was added Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhenzong's accession he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 坐交結王繼恩，貶忠武軍節度行軍司馬。

translations.literal: For associating with Wang Ji'en, he was demoted to staff adjutant of the Zhongwu Army military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of colluding with Wang Ji'en, he was demoted to staff adjutant of the Zhongwu Army command.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，起為殿中少監。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping he was recalled and appointed Vice Director of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping (999) he was recalled and appointed vice director of the palace.

sentences.zh: 會詔群臣言邊事，昌齡求面陳事機，不報。

translations.literal: When an edict summoned the ministers to speak on frontier affairs, Changling requested to present the situation in person; he received no response.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict summoned ministers to speak on frontier affairs, Changling asked to present the situation in person, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 王均之亂，命知梓州。

translations.literal: During Wang Jun's rebellion he was ordered to govern Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Jun's rebellion he was appointed prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 知雜御史範正辭劾其廣舶宿犯，亟代還，知河陽。

translations.literal: Supervising Miscellaneous Censor Fan Zhengci impeached him for old offenses involving Guangzhou shipping; he was quickly replaced and recalled, and appointed prefect of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising miscellaneous censor Fan Zhengci impeached him for old offenses involving Guangzhou shipping. He was quickly replaced and recalled, then appointed prefect of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 丁外艱，起復，奉朝請，以風恙求領小郡，復得光州，就改光祿卿。

translations.literal: When his father died he was recalled from mourning; as gentleman attendant at court he pleaded illness from wind ailment to request a small prefecture, again obtained Guangzhou, and was concurrently changed to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he was recalled from mourning to serve as gentleman attendant at court. Citing wind ailment, he asked for a small prefecture, was again given Guangzhou, and was concurrently made grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 疾，不能治事。

translations.literal: He fell ill and could not administer affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and could no longer administer affairs.

sentences.zh: 轉運使以聞，命守本官分司西京。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner reported it; he was ordered to retain his existing office and serve in nominal capacity in the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner reported this, and he was ordered to retain his existing rank while serving in nominal capacity in the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 尋請致仕，真宗曰：「昌齡素無清譽。」

translations.literal: Soon he requested retirement; Emperor Zhenzong said: "Changling has never had a reputation for integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he requested retirement. Emperor Zhenzong said, "Changling has never had a reputation for integrity."

sentences.zh: 乃授秘書監，遂其請。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Director of the Secretariat, granting his request.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed director of the secretariat, granting his request.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年，卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu he died at age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu (1008) he died at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 廢朝，錄子虞卿試將作監主簿。

translations.literal: Court audiences were suspended; his son Yuqing was recorded for trial appointment as principal clerk of the Directorate of Imperial Works.
translations.idiomatic: Court audiences were suspended, and his son Yuqing was granted a trial appointment as principal clerk of the directorate of imperial works.

sentences.zh: 昌齡兄昌圖至國子博士，弟昌言至太子中舍。

translations.literal: Changling's elder brother Changtu rose to Erudite of the Directorate of Education; his younger brother Changyan rose to Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Changling's elder brother Changtu rose to erudite of the directorate of education, and his younger brother Changyan to attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 昌言子晉卿、仲卿、耀卿，並進士及第，晉卿為秘書丞。

translations.literal: Changyan's sons Jinqing, Zhongqing, and Yaoqing all passed the jinshi examination; Jinqing became Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Changyan's sons Jinqing, Zhongqing, and Yaoqing all passed the jinshi examination; Jinqing became secretary of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 從子 紘

translations.literal: Nephew Hong.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Hong.

sentences.zh: 紘，字仲綱。

translations.literal: Hong, style name Zhonggang.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, courtesy name Zhonggang.

sentences.zh: 父克明，仕至提點廣東刑獄。

translations.literal: His father Keming served up to Intendant of Judicial Affairs for Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Keming had risen to Intendant of Judicial Affairs for Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 紘，進士及第，試秘書省校書郎、知歙縣。

translations.literal: Hong passed the jinshi examination, tried as Collator in the Secretariat and prefect of She County.
translations.idiomatic: Hong passed the jinshi examination and was appointed collator in the Secretariat and magistrate of She County.

sentences.zh: 地產黃金，民輸以代賦，後金竭，責其賦如故。

translations.literal: The region produced gold; the people paid it in lieu of tax; later when gold was exhausted, their tax was charged as before.
translations.idiomatic: The county produced gold, which the people had paid in lieu of regular taxes; when the gold ran out, the tax burden remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 紘奏罷之。

translations.literal: Hong memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Hong memorialized to end the practice.

sentences.zh: 歷知於潛、剡縣，治有惠愛。

translations.literal: He successively administered Yuqian and Shan counties; his governance had benevolence and affection.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as magistrate of Yuqian and Shan counties, governing with kindness and solicitude.

sentences.zh: 御史知雜呂夷簡薦之，改著作佐郎、監丹陽縣酒稅，知靈池縣。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Charge Lü Yijian recommended him; changed to Assistant Editor, supervised Danyang County wine tax, prefect of Lingchi County.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Charge Lü Yijian recommended him; he was made Assistant Editor, put in charge of the wine tax at Danyang County, and appointed magistrate of Lingchi County.

sentences.zh: 劉均、蔡齊舉為御史臺推直官，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: Liu Jun and Cai Qi jointly recommended him as a direct officer of the Censorate and he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jun and Cai Qi jointly recommended him as a direct officer of the Censorate, and he was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時召成都府樂工許朝天等補教坊，紘言：「陛下即位，尚未能顯嚴穴之士，而首召伶人，非所以廣德美於天下。」

translations.literal: At the time musicians of Chengdu Prefecture, Xu Chaotian and others, were summoned to fill posts in the Music Bureau; Hong said: "Your Majesty has taken the throne but has not yet been able to display men of seclusion from cave and cliff, while first summoning entertainers—this is not the way to spread virtue and beauty throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court summoned Xu Chaotian and other musicians of Chengdu Prefecture to fill posts in the Music Bureau. Hong said, "Your Majesty has just acceded to the throne but has not yet been able to call forth worthy men living in seclusion, while summoning entertainers first—this is not how to spread virtue and excellence throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 朝天等遂罷歸。

translations.literal: Chaotian and the others were then dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Chaotian and the others were then dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attending censor in the palace.

sentences.zh: 閤門使王遵度領皇城，遣卒刺事，告賈人有為契丹間諜者，捕繫皇城司按劾。

translations.literal: Gate Attendant Wang Zundu commanded the Imperial City and sent soldiers to investigate affairs; they reported that a merchant was a Khitan spy; he was seized and imprisoned, and the Imperial City Office conducted the inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Gate attendant Wang Zundu commanded the Imperial City and sent soldiers to investigate; they reported that a merchant was a Khitan spy. The man was seized and imprisoned, and the Imperial City Office conducted the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 命紘覆訊，紘悉得其冤，抵卒罪，降遵度曹州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: Hong was ordered to reexamine the case; Hong fully established their innocence, punished the soldiers, and demoted Zundu to military controller of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was ordered to reexamine the case. He fully established the prisoners' innocence, punished the soldiers, and demoted Zundu to military controller of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 判三司開拆司。

translations.literal: Adjudicated the Three Bureaus Opening and Sorting Office.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of the Three Bureaus' Opening and Sorting Office.

sentences.zh: 輔郡旱，流星墜西南有聲，會僧禳於文德殿，紘奏曰：「文德殿布政會朝之正位，每災異，輒聚緇黃讚唄於其間，何以示中外？」

translations.literal: The auxiliary capital suffered drought; a meteor fell in the southwest with a sound; monks performed exorcism rites at Wende Hall; Hong memorialized: "Wende Hall is the proper seat where government is promulgated and court is held; whenever there are calamities and anomalies, black-robed and yellow-robed ones gather to chant praises within it—how can this be shown to court and commoners?"
translations.idiomatic: During a drought in the auxiliary capital a meteor fell in the southwest with a loud crash; monks were performing exorcism rites in Wende Hall when Hong memorialized: "Wende Hall is the throne room where policy is proclaimed and court convened—yet at every sign of calamity monks and priests gather there to chant. What message does this send to the empire?"

sentences.zh: 改鹽鐵判官，歷梓州、陝西、河北路轉運使，遷侍御史。

translations.literal: Changed to Salt and Iron Commissioner; successively served as transport commissioner for Zizhou, Shaanxi, and Hebei circuits; promoted to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Salt and Iron Commissioner, then served successively as transport commissioner for the Zizhou, Shaanxi, and Hebei circuits before being promoted to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 建言：「西北久通好，士習安佚，不知戰陣之法。

translations.literal: He submitted advice: "The northwest has long been at peace; soldiers are accustomed to ease and rest, not knowing the methods of battle formations.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a proposal: "The northwest has enjoyed peace so long that troops have grown complacent and no longer know how to fight.

sentences.zh: 宜擇良將，練精卒，去冗惰，實倉廩，豐財用，為守禦備。」

translations.literal: One should select good generals, drill elite soldiers, remove redundant laziness, fill granaries, enrich financial resources, and make preparations for defense."
translations.idiomatic: We should choose able commanders, train crack troops, cut dead weight, fill the granaries, strengthen finances, and ready ourselves for defense."

sentences.zh: 舉种世衡等數人，及奏罷貢餘物遺近臣。

translations.literal: He recommended several men including Zhong Shiheng, and also memorialized to abolish surplus tribute goods given to close ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended several men including Zhong Shiheng and also memorialized to end the practice of showering surplus tribute goods on the emperor's favorites.

sentences.zh: 遷知雜事、權同判流內銓。

translations.literal: Promoted to censor-in-charge, acting concurrent adjudicator of the Registry of Current Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor-in-charge and given acting concurrent charge of the registry of current appointments.

sentences.zh: 為三司度支副使，使契丹。

translations.literal: Made Vice Commissioner of the Three Bureaus Revenue Bureau, envoy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Commissioner of the Revenue Bureau under the Three Bureaus and went as envoy to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 故事，奉使者以皇城卒二人與偕，察其舉措，使者悉姑息以避中傷。

translations.literal: By precedent, envoys on mission were accompanied by two Imperial City soldiers to observe their conduct; envoys all indulged to avoid being slandered.
translations.idiomatic: By custom each diplomatic envoy was accompanied by two Imperial City guards who monitored his behavior; envoys typically indulged them to avoid malicious reports.

sentences.zh: 前此劉隨為所誣，坐貶，久未復。

translations.literal: Earlier Liu Sui was slandered by them, demoted for it, and long not restored.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sui had earlier been falsely denounced by such guards, demoted, and not restored for a long time.

sentences.zh: 紘使還，具言其枉，稍徙隨南京。

translations.literal: When Hong returned from his mission, he fully stated Liu's injustice; Liu was slightly transferred to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from his mission Hong fully reported Liu's wrongful treatment, and Liu was gradually transferred to Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 除天章閣待制、河北都轉運使，遷刑部郎中，還，同知通進、銀臺司，進龍圖閣直學士、知秦州，卒。

translations.literal: Granted Tianzhang Pavilion Attendant-in-Waiting, Hebei Chief Transport Commissioner; promoted Bureau Director in Ministry of Justice; returning, concurrently administered Tongjin and Yintai bureaus; advanced to Dragon Diagram Pavilion Academic Scholar, prefect of Qin Prefecture; died.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Tianzhang Pavilion Attendant-in-Waiting and Chief Transport Commissioner for Hebei, promoted to Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice, and upon returning concurrently administered the Tongjin and Yintai bureaus; he was advanced to Dragon Diagram Pavilion Academic Scholar and appointed prefect of Qin Prefecture, where he died.

sentences.zh: 紘方介有吏材，篤於交遊，與劉顏為友，顏死，移任子恩官其子。

translations.literal: Hong was upright and had administrative talent, devoted in friendship; he was friends with Liu Yan; when Yan died, he transferred the grace of an official post to Yan's son.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was upright and capable in administration, and deeply loyal in friendship; when his friend Liu Yan died, he obtained an official appointment for Yan's son.

sentences.zh: 弟緯，起家三班借職，杜衍薦為閤門祗候，鎮戎軍瓦亭砦都監。

translations.literal: Younger brother Wei, starting from Third Rank Bureau provisional appointment; Du Yan recommended him as Gatekeeper Attendant, Chief Supervisor of Wating Stockade at Zhenrong Army.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Wei entered service with a provisional Third Rank Bureau appointment; recommended by Du Yan, he became Gatekeeper Attendant and chief supervisor of Wating Stockade at Zhenrong Army.

sentences.zh: 積勞累遷至河北緣邊安撫副使。

translations.literal: Accumulating merit he was repeatedly promoted to Hebei Frontier Pacification Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Through accumulated merit he rose to Vice Commissioner for Hebei Frontier Pacification.

sentences.zh: 韓琦薦知保州，以左騏驥使、榮州刺史知雄州。

translations.literal: Han Qi recommended him as prefect of Bao Prefecture; as Left Pacer and Prefect of Rong Prefecture he administered Xiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Han Qi, he served as prefect of Bao Prefecture and later as Left Pacer and nominal prefect of Rong while governing Xiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 治兵頗嚴，不事廚傳，數與宦者爭利害。

translations.literal: He drilled troops quite strictly, did not indulge in official hospitality, and repeatedly contended with eunuchs over interests.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled his troops rigorously, eschewed lavish official entertainment, and repeatedly clashed with eunuchs over policy.

sentences.zh: 積公使錢貯米三千斛為常平倉，奏下其法他州。

translations.literal: He amassed public envoy funds to store three thousand bushels of rice as a granary for stabilizing prices; memorialized to extend this law to other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He accumulated public funds to stock three thousand bushels of rice in a price-stabilization granary and memorialized to extend the practice to other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 遷西上閤門使，留再任，卒。

translations.literal: Promoted to Western Upper Gate Envoy; retained for another term; died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Western Upper Gate Envoy, kept on for a second term, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子師中至天章閣待制。

translations.literal: His son Shizhong reached Tianzhang Pavilion Attendant-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shizhong rose to Tianzhang Pavilion Attendant-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 趙安仁

translations.literal: Zhao Anren
translations.idiomatic: The biography continues with Zhao Anren.

sentences.zh: 趙安仁，字樂道，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Zhao Anren, style name Ledao, a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Anren, courtesy name Ledao, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖武唐，虢州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Wutang was prefect of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Wutang had served as prefect of Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父孚，字大信。

translations.literal: His father Fu, style name Daxin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fu, courtesy name Daxin.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初，舉進士，調補開封尉。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande under Zhou, he passed the jinshi examination and was assigned to supplement Kaifeng police officer.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Xiande era under Later Zhou he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a Kaifeng police officer.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，為浦江令，持父喪，服闋，攝永寧令。

translations.literal: During Qiande he was magistrate of Pujiang; observed mourning for his father; when mourning ended, acted as magistrate of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande era he served as magistrate of Pujiang; after his father's death he observed mourning, and when the period ended he served as acting magistrate of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 會親征太原，部送本邑糧饋，民懷其惠，列狀以聞，即真授其任，擢宗正丞。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally campaigned against Taiyuan, he organized delivery of grain provisions from his district; the people cherished his kindness and submitted a collective petition reporting it; he was immediately confirmed in his appointment and promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor personally marched on Taiyuan, Fu organized the delivery of grain from his district; grateful locals petitioned the throne on his behalf, and he was immediately confirmed in his post and promoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，初置衣庫，令孚主之。

translations.literal: During Kaibao, the Garment Storehouse was first established and Fu was ordered to administer it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era the imperial Garment Storehouse was first established, with Fu placed in charge.

sentences.zh: 俄坐事連逮抵罪，語見《趙普傳》。

translations.literal: Soon for an affair he was implicated and punished; the account is in the Biography of Zhao Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was implicated in a crime and punished; details appear in the Biography of Zhao Pu.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，起為國子監丞、知袁州。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, he was recalled as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and prefect of Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On Taizong's accession he was recalled to serve as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and prefect of Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 還，知開封府司錄參軍事，受詔與殿中侍御史柴成務、供奉官葛彥恭、殿直郭載行視黃河，分南北岸按行，復遙堤以紓湍決。

translations.literal: Returning, he was made Recorder of the Kaifeng Prefecture office; ordered together with Attending Censor Chai Chengwu, Attendant-in-Waiting Ge Yangong, and Palace Direct Guo Zai to inspect the Yellow River, divided into south and north banks to proceed along them, and restored distant dikes to ease violent breaches.
translations.idiomatic: After returning he served as recorder of the Kaifeng Prefecture office and was ordered, together with Attending Censor Chai Chengwu, Attendant-in-Waiting Ge Yangong, and Palace Direct Guo Zai, to inspect the Yellow River; they surveyed both banks and restored distant dikes to relieve flooding.

sentences.zh: 孚言治遙堤不如分水勢，於是建議於澶、滑二州立分水之制。

translations.literal: Fu said governing distant dikes was inferior to dividing water force; thus he proposed establishing a water-dividing system at Chao and Hua prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Fu argued that distant dikes were less effective than channeling the water's force and proposed a diversion system at Chao and Hua prefectures.

sentences.zh: 時決河未平，重惜民力而寢焉。

translations.literal: At the time the Yellow River breach was not yet settled; they valued people's labor highly and let the proposal sleep.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the river breach had not yet been contained, and the court, reluctant to strain the people's labor, set the proposal aside.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議行封禪，孚上《封禪頌》，召拜秘書丞，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: Court deliberated performing the feng and shan rites; Fu submitted "Ode to the Feng and Shan"; summoned and invested as Secretariat Director, granted red fish insignia.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated performing the feng and shan rites, Fu submitted an "Ode to the Feng and Shan"; he was summoned and appointed Secretariat Director and granted red fish insignia.

sentences.zh: 受詔鞫開封獄，得其非辜者，即日授推官。

translations.literal: Ordered to investigate Kaifeng prison cases, finding those not guilty, he was on the same day appointed investigating magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Tasked with reviewing Kaifeng prison cases, he uncovered wrongful convictions and was appointed investigating magistrate that same day.

sentences.zh: 遷監察御史，出知舒州，改殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Promoted to Supervising Censor; sent out as prefect of Shu Prefecture; changed to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supervising Censor, appointed prefect of Shu Prefecture, and later transferred to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，詔詢文武禦戎之策。

translations.literal: During Yongxi, an edict inquired about civil and military strategies for defending against barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era the throne solicited civil and military strategies for frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 孚奏議曰：「臣愚以為不用干戈，不勞飛輓，為萬世之利者，敢獻其說，惟明主擇之。

translations.literal: Fu submitted a memorial saying: "This subject foolishly considers that without using weapons, without troubling rapid transport, what brings benefit for ten thousand generations—I dare present my view; may the enlightened ruler choose.
translations.idiomatic: Fu submitted a memorial stating: "Your servant believes that what would benefit posterity without drawing swords or straining the transport corps deserves a hearing, and I beg the wise sovereign to weigh my proposal.

sentences.zh: 古者兵交使在其間，雖飛矢在上，走驛在下，蓋信義不可廢也。

translations.literal: In antiquity when armies clashed, envoys passed between them; though flying arrows were above and racing post-horses below, trust and righteousness could not be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity even when armies clashed, diplomatic envoys still passed between the lines; though arrows flew overhead and couriers raced below, good faith was never discarded.

sentences.zh: 昔苗民逆命，帝乃誕敷文德，而有苗格。

translations.literal: Formerly the Miao people rebelled against orders; the Emperor then broadly spread civil virtue, and the Miao submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao defied the throne, the emperor spread civil virtue abroad, and they submitted.

sentences.zh: 又仲尼曰：『有能一日克己復禮，天下歸仁。』

translations.literal: Moreover Confucius said: "If one can in one day restrain himself and return to ritual, all under Heaven will return to benevolence."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius also said: "If a man can for a single day restrain himself and return to ritual, the empire will turn toward benevolence."

sentences.zh: 只如幷門一方，歷代難取，聖襟英斷，一舉成功。

translations.literal: Take only the Bing region—for generations hard to take; the sage bosom was heroic and decisive, succeeding in one move.
translations.idiomatic: Consider Bingzhou alone—dynasty after dynasty had failed to take it, yet Your Majesty's resolute judgment seized it in a single stroke.

sentences.zh: 當其逆城危於累卵，生聚懷伏，而陛下猶遣通事舍人薛文寶入城諭之。

translations.literal: When their rebellious city was as perilous as a pile of eggs, the living and gathered cowered in submission, yet Your Majesty still sent the Transmission Affairs Commissioner Xue Wenbao into the city to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel city hung by a thread and its people cowered in dread, Your Majesty still sent Transmission Affairs Commissioner Xue Wenbao into the city to offer terms.

sentences.zh: 日者北邊未賓，全燕猶梗，再興軍旅，將復土疆。

translations.literal: Recently the northern frontier has not submitted; all of Yan still obstructs; again raising armies and troops, about to recover territory.
translations.idiomatic: Now the north has not yet submitted, all of Yan still holds out, and once again armies are raised to recover lost territory.

sentences.zh: 臣竊計屯戍邊陲，故非獲已，暴露原野，豈是願為？

translations.literal: This subject privately calculates that garrisoning the frontier borders is indeed not obtained willingly; exposed in wild fields—how could that be what one wishes to do?
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that border garrisons exist only because no alternative remains—who would willingly endure exposure on the open steppe?

sentences.zh: 欲望朝廷通達國信，近鑒唐高祖之降禮，遠法周古公之讓地。

translations.literal: I desire that the court communicate the nation's trust, take as a near mirror Tang Gaozu's descending rites, and far model the Zhou ancient duke's yielding of land.
translations.idiomatic: I hope the court will convey its good faith clearly—taking warning from Emperor Gaozu of Tang's humiliating concessions, and emulating in distant antiquity the ancient Zhou duke's relinquishment of territory.

sentences.zh: 聖人以百姓之心為心，君子見幾而作，諭以禍福，示以恩威，議定邊疆，永息征戰。

translations.literal: Sages take the hearts of the common people as their heart; gentlemen see the subtle sign and act, instruct with fortune and calamity, display favor and severity, settle the borderlands by deliberation, and forever cease campaigns and battles.
translations.idiomatic: Sages align their will with that of the people; a worthy minister acts when he reads the signs. Explain the consequences of fortune and disaster, show both kindness and firm authority, fix the boundaries through negotiation, and bring war to a permanent end.

sentences.zh: 養民事天，濟時利物，莫過於此。

translations.literal: Nourishing the people and serving Heaven, helping the age and benefiting things—nothing surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing would do more to nurture the people, honor Heaven, serve the times, and benefit the realm than this course.

sentences.zh: 臣又計彼雖嗜好不同，然去危就安，厭勞喜逸，亦人情之所同也。」

translations.literal: Your subject also calculates that though they differ in tastes, yet leaving danger and approaching safety, tiring of toil and delighting in ease—this too is what human feelings share alike."
translations.idiomatic: I further reckon that though their customs differ, the wish to flee danger for safety and labor for rest is universal human nature."

sentences.zh: 上嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor expressed his approval.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，廷策貢士，而安仁預為考會，賜金紫，因顧安仁問孚年幾，安仁曰：「臣父年六十二。」

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, at the palace examination of tribute scholars, Anren participated in the review committee and was granted gold seal and purple robe. Thereupon the emperor turned to Anren and asked Fu's age. Anren said: "My father's age is sixty-two."
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi period, at the palace examination for presented scholars, Anren served on the grading committee and received the gold seal and purple robe. The emperor glanced at Anren and asked how old Fu was. Anren replied, "My father is sixty-two."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「孚，名士也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Fu is a renowned scholar."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Fu is a man of distinguished reputation."

sentences.zh: 亟召對，亦賜金紫。

translations.literal: He immediately summoned him for audience and also bestowed gold seal and purple robe.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was promptly summoned for an audience and given the gold seal and purple robe as well.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒。

translations.literal: The next year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 安仁生而穎悟，幼時執筆能大字，十三通經傳大旨，早以文藝稱。

translations.literal: Anren was born keen and quick; in youth taking the brush he could write large characters; at thirteen he mastered the great purport of the classics and commentaries; early he was famed for literary arts.
translations.idiomatic: Anren was bright from birth. As a child he could wield the brush and write large characters; by thirteen he had grasped the main themes of the classics and was already known for his literary talent.

sentences.zh: 趙普、沈倫、李昉、石熙載咸推獎之。

translations.literal: Zhao Pu, Shen Lun, Li Fang, and Shi Xizai all praised and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pu, Shen Lun, Li Fang, and Shi Xizai all extolled and commended him.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，登進士第，補梓州榷鹽院判官，以親老弗果往。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed salt monopoly subprefect at Zizhou, but because his parents were old he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxi 2 he passed the jinshi examinations and was assigned as judge of the Zizhou Salt Monopoly Office, but he never took up the post because his parents were elderly.

sentences.zh: 會國子監刻《五經正義》板本，以安仁善楷隸，遂奏留書之。

translations.literal: It happened that the Directorate of Education was carving blocks for the Correct Meaning of the Five Classics; because Anren excelled at regular and clerical script, they memorialized to retain him to write it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Directorate of Education was cutting woodblocks for the Correct Meaning of the Five Classics, Anren's skill in standard and clerical script led to a petition that he be kept on to do the writing.

sentences.zh: 歷大理評事、光祿寺丞，召試翰林，以著作佐郎直集賢院，賜緋。

translations.literal: He served successively as reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; summoned for Hanlin examination, appointed Left Assistant Gentleman of Palace Library on duty at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, granted scarlet robe.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of judicial reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review and vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then passed a Hanlin examination and was made Left Assistant Gentleman in the Palace Library, serving on duty at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, with the scarlet robe conferred.

sentences.zh: 時王侯、內戚家多以銘誄為託。

translations.literal: At the time royal princes and inner consort kin often entrusted him with epitaphs and dirges.
translations.idiomatic: Princes and imperial in-laws often commissioned him to write epitaphs and funeral eulogies.

sentences.zh: 太宗製九紘琴、五紘阮，時多獻賦頌，上嘉文物之盛，悉閱覽，訂其工拙。

translations.literal: Taizong made the nine-string qin and five-string ruan; at the time many presented rhapsodies and encomia; the emperor rejoiced in the flourish of cultural artifacts, perused them all, and judged their craftsmanship and crudeness.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong had the nine-string qin and five-string ruan made, many submitted fu and song in praise. Delighted by this flowering of culture, the emperor read them all and weighed their literary merit.

sentences.zh: 時稱安仁、李宗諤、楊億辭雅贍，召詣中書獎諭。

translations.literal: At the time Anren, Li Zong'e, and Yang Yi were called elegant and ample in diction; they were summoned to the Secretariat for reward and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Anren, Li Zong'e, and Yang Yi were then hailed for their refined and copious prose, and were summoned to the Secretariat to receive commendation.

sentences.zh: 翌日，改遷太常丞。

translations.literal: The next day, he was transferred to be vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The following day he was reassigned as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，拜右正言，預重修《太祖實錄》。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong ascended the throne, Anren was appointed Right Remonstrator and took part in the renewed compilation of Veritable Records of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Upon Zhenzong's accession, he was made Right Remonstrator and helped revise the Veritable Records of Emperor Taizu.

sentences.zh: 上出師大名，安仁上疏曰：「臣以為有急務者三，大要者五。

translations.literal: When the emperor marched out to Daming, Anren submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject considers there are three urgent tasks and five major essentials.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor set out for Daming at the head of the army, Anren submitted a memorial: "I believe there are three urgent priorities and five broad essentials.

sentences.zh: 急務三者：其一，激勵戎臣，舉勸懲之典；

translations.literal: The three urgent tasks: first, to inspire and encourage military officers, applying the statutes of reward and punishment;
translations.idiomatic: The three urgent tasks are these: first, rouse the frontier commanders and enforce the standards of merit and discipline;

sentences.zh: 其二，振救邊民，行優恤之惠；

translations.literal: second, to revive and rescue border people, carrying out preferential relief;
translations.idiomatic: second, relieve the border population and extend them generous aid;

sentences.zh: 其三，車駕還京，重神武之威。

translations.literal: third, when the imperial carriage returns to the capital, restore the majesty of divine martial prowess.
translations.idiomatic: third, when Your Majesty returns to the capital, restore the awe of imperial military might.

sentences.zh: 大要五者：其一，選將略；

translations.literal: The five major essentials: first, selecting generals' stratagems;
translations.idiomatic: The five broad essentials are these: first, choose commanders for their strategic skill;

sentences.zh: 其二，持兵勢；

translations.literal: second, maintaining military momentum;
translations.idiomatic: second, sustain military strength;

sentences.zh: 其三，求軍謀；

translations.literal: third, seeking army stratagems;
translations.idiomatic: third, seek sound military counsel;

sentences.zh: 其四，修軍政；

translations.literal: fourth, repairing army administration;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, reform military governance;

sentences.zh: 其五，愛民力。」

translations.literal: fifth, cherishing the people's strength."
translations.idiomatic: fifth, conserve the people's resources and labor."

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，同知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping, he was co-director of the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianping 3 he served as co-examiner for the civil service tests.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知制誥，副夏侯嶠巡撫江南，還，知審刑院。

translations.literal: Before long, he became drafter of edicts, assisted Xiahou Qiao in inspecting Jiangnan, returned, and directed the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was made drafter of edicts, accompanied Xiahou Qiao on an inspection tour of the Jiangnan region, and upon return was put in charge of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 嘗有將校笞所部卒死，罪議大辟。

translations.literal: Once a military officer flogged a subordinate soldier to death; the crime was debated as capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Once a commander beat a soldier under his command to death, and the case was argued as a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 安仁以軍中之令，非嚴不整，遂獲免死。

translations.literal: Anren argued that in the army's commands, without severity there is no order, and thus he obtained exemption from death.
translations.idiomatic: Anren held that military discipline requires strictness if troops are to remain in order, and on that ground the man was spared execution.

sentences.zh: 繼判尚書刑部兼制置群牧使，同知三班、審官院。

translations.literal: Subsequently he served as concurrent judge of the Ministry of Justice in the Department of State Affairs and commissioner for setting up the herds; co-director of the Three Ranks and the Bureau of Review.
translations.idiomatic: He then served concurrently as judge of the Ministry of Justice, commissioner for horse herds, and co-director of the Three Ranks Office and the Bureau of Review.

sentences.zh: 景德初，翰林學士梁顥召對，詢及當世臺閣人物，上稱安仁文行。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingde, Hanlin academician Liang Hao was summoned for audience; asked about contemporary eminent officials, the emperor praised Anren's literary conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era, when Hanlin academician Liang Hao was summoned to audience and asked about leading court figures of the day, the emperor singled out Anren's literary talent and integrity.

sentences.zh: 尋顥卒，即以安仁為工部員外郎，充翰林學士。

translations.literal: Soon Liang Hao died, and Anren was immediately made Vice Minister of Works and appointed Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Hao died shortly afterward, Anren was promoted to Vice Minister of Works and appointed Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 初，孚極陳和好之利。

translations.literal: At first, Fu had strongly stated the benefits of harmony and accord.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Fu had argued forcefully for the advantages of peace.

sentences.zh: 至是，安仁從幸澶州，會北邊請盟，首命安仁撰答書，又獨記太祖時聘問書式。

translations.literal: At this time, Anren followed the emperor's visit to Chanzhou; meeting the northern border's request for alliance, he was first ordered to draft the reply letter and alone recorded the format of envoys' letters from Taizu's time.
translations.idiomatic: Now Anren accompanied the emperor to Chanzhou. When the north sought a treaty, he was first charged with drafting the reply and was the only one who still remembered the diplomatic letter forms used in Taizu's reign.

sentences.zh: 遼使韓杞至，道命接伴，凡覲見儀制，多所裁定。

translations.literal: When Liao envoy Han Qi arrived, the court ordered him to receive and accompany; for all audience rites and protocols, he judged and settled many points.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liao envoy Han Qi arrived, Anren was ordered to serve as his host, and he settled many questions of ceremony and protocol for the imperial audience.

sentences.zh: 館舍夕飲，杞舉橙子曰：「此果嘗見高麗貢。」

translations.literal: At an evening drink in the guest lodge, Qi raised an orange and said: "This fruit I once saw presented as tribute from Goryeo."
translations.idiomatic: At an evening gathering in the lodge, Qi held up an orange and said, "I once saw this fruit sent as tribute from Goryeo."

sentences.zh: 安仁曰：「橙橘產吳、楚，朝廷職方掌天下圖經，凡他國所產靡不知也。

translations.literal: Anren said: "Oranges and tangerines are produced in Wu and Chu; the Court's Bureau of Maps and Registers holds the gazetteers of all under Heaven—whatever other states produce, nothing is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Anren replied, "Oranges and tangerines come from Wu and Chu. The Directorate of Maps maintains gazetteers of the entire realm and knows the products of every foreign land.

sentences.zh: 今給事中呂祐之嘗使高麗，未聞有橙柚。」

translations.literal: Now Supervising Secretary Lü Youzhi once served as envoy to Goryeo—nothing was heard of oranges or pomelos."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Lü Youzhi served as envoy to Goryeo, and he reported no oranges or pomelos there."

sentences.zh: 杞失於誇誕，有愧色。

translations.literal: Qi lost in boasting and exaggeration, showing an ashamed countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Qi, caught in his boast, looked ashamed.

sentences.zh: 杞既受襲衣之賜，且以長為解，將辭復左衽。

translations.literal: Qi having received the gift of ceremonial robes, and using length as excuse, when about to take leave again wore left lapel.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving the gift of court robes, Qi tried to excuse himself on the grounds of their size and, when preparing to leave, put his robe on with the left lapel forward.

sentences.zh: 安仁曰：「君將升殿受還書，天顏咫尺，如不衣所賜之衣，可乎？」

translations.literal: Anren said: "You are about to ascend the hall to receive the return letter; the imperial countenance is within a foot—if you do not wear the robes that were bestowed, is that acceptable?"
translations.idiomatic: Anren said, "You are about to enter the hall to receive the reply letter. The emperor's face will be before you—is it fitting to appear without wearing the robes he gave you?"

sentences.zh: 杞乃服以入。

translations.literal: Qi then wore them and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Qi put the robes on properly and went in.

sentences.zh: 及姚東之至，又令安仁接伴。

translations.literal: When Yao Dongzhi arrived, again Anren was ordered to receive and accompany.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Dongzhi arrived, Anren was again appointed to receive him.

sentences.zh: 東之談次，頗矜兵強戰勝。

translations.literal: In the course of Dongzhi's conversation, he rather prided himself on strong troops and victorious battles.
translations.idiomatic: During conversation, Dongzhi was rather boastful about his army's strength and battlefield victories.

sentences.zh: 安仁曰：「老氏云：『佳兵者不祥之器，聖人不得已而用之。』

translations.literal: Anren said: "Laozi says: 'Fine weapons are inauspicious implements; the sage uses them only when he has no choice.
translations.idiomatic: Anren said, "Laozi wrote: 'Outstanding weapons are ill-omened tools; the sage employs them only when he must.

sentences.zh: 勝而不美，而美之者，是樂殺人也，樂殺人者不得志於天下。」

translations.literal: Victory without beautifying it—yet he who beautifies it delights in killing people; he who delights in killing people cannot achieve his aim under Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: To win a war without celebrating it is best; to celebrate victory is to delight in killing, and one who delights in killing will never prevail in the world.'

sentences.zh: 東之自是不敢復言。

translations.literal: Dongzhi from then dared not speak again.
translations.idiomatic: After that Dongzhi did not dare raise the subject again.

sentences.zh: 王繼忠將兵陷沒，不能死節而反事之，東之屢稱其材。

translations.literal: Wang Jizhong leading troops was captured; unable to die for integrity yet instead serving them, Dongzhi repeatedly praised his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jizhong had surrendered with his troops rather than die loyal to the Song, yet had gone over to serve the Liao; Dongzhi repeatedly praised his abilities.

sentences.zh: 安仁曰：「繼忠早事藩邸，聞其稍謹，不知其他。」

translations.literal: Anren said: "Jizhong early served the princely establishment; I heard he was somewhat careful—I know nothing of the rest."
translations.idiomatic: Anren replied, "Jizhong served our prince's household long ago, and I heard he was reasonably conscientious—but beyond that I know nothing."

sentences.zh: 其敏於酬對，切中事機，類如此。

translations.literal: His quickness in repartee, hitting the mark of the occasion—things were mostly like this.
translations.idiomatic: His sharpness in debate and his knack for striking the right note at the right moment were typical of exchanges like these.

sentences.zh: 時論翕然，稱其得體，上益器之，自是有意柄用。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion united in acclaim, calling his conduct appropriate; the emperor increasingly treasured him, and from then intended to employ him in power.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion rallied to praise his tact, and the emperor valued him all the more; from that point he was marked for high office.

sentences.zh: 安仁又集和好以來事宜，及采古事，作《戴斗懷柔錄》三卷以獻。

translations.literal: Anren also gathered affairs since harmony and accord, and collecting ancient precedents, composed Records of Wearing the Dipper and Cherishing Softness in three fascicles to present.
translations.idiomatic: Anren also compiled matters arising since the peace and drew on ancient examples to write the Records of Wearing the Dipper and Cherishing Softness in three fascicles, which he presented to the throne.

sentences.zh: 二年春，又與晁迥等同知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, again with Chao Kui and others he co-directed the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year he again served as co-examiner with Chao Kui and others.

sentences.zh: 三年，以右諫議大夫參知政事，俄修國史。

translations.literal: In the third year, as Right Supervisory Censor he became Vice Grand Councilor; soon he compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Vice Grand Councilor with the rank of Right Supervisory Censor and soon took charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，議封禪，與王欽若並為泰山經制度置使、判兗州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong Xiangfu, when feng and shan were debated, with Wang Qinruo together he became commissioner for arranging rites at Mount Tai and prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dazhong Xiangfu era, when the court debated the feng and shan rites, he and Wang Qinruo were jointly appointed commissioners for Mount Tai ritual arrangements and made prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 禮畢，復拜工部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the rites were complete, again appointed Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites were completed he was again appointed Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 內外書詔有切要者，必經其裁。

translations.literal: Important internal and external documents and edicts necessarily passed through his judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Important edicts and memorials, whether domestic or foreign, all required his editorial approval.

sentences.zh: 進秩刑部。

translations.literal: Promoted in rank to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 五年，以兵部侍郎仍兼修史，奉祀，又同知禮儀院。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, as Vice Minister of War still concurrently compiling history, performing sacrifices, again co-director of the Court of Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, while serving as Vice Minister of War and still compiling the history, he also assisted in state sacrifices and became co-director of the Court of Ritual.

sentences.zh: 八年，知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he directed the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he served as chief examiner.

sentences.zh: 三典春闈，擇士平允，是故獨無譏誚，上再賜詩嘉之。

translations.literal: Three times presiding over the spring gate, selecting scholars fairly and evenhandedly—for this alone there was no blame or ridicule; the emperor twice bestowed poems in praise.
translations.idiomatic: Having presided over the metropolitan examinations three times and selected candidates with scrupulous fairness, he alone escaped criticism, and the emperor twice honored him with commendatory poems.

sentences.zh: 尋知兼宗正卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed director and concurrently Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon put in charge of the Imperial Clan Court as well.

sentences.zh: 舊制，宮闈令，凡有議奏與寺連署。

translations.literal: Under the old system, for inner palace orders, whenever there were deliberations and memorials, joint signature with the court was required.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rules, palace matters submitted for discussion had to be jointly signed by the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 上以安仁舊德，俾知寺，以次列狀取裁。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of Anren's longstanding virtue, had him direct the court, with memorials listed in order for his decision.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Anren's long service and reputation, the emperor put him in charge of the court so that petitions could be submitted in proper order for his ruling.

sentences.zh: 寺掌玉牒屬籍，梁周翰始創其制而未備，安仁重加詳定，又為《仙源積慶圖》，皆統例精簡。

translations.literal: The court managed jade registers and genealogical rolls; Liang Zhouhan first established the system but it was incomplete; Anren added detailed revision, and also compiled Chart of Accumulated Blessings from the Immortal Source—all with systematic categories refined and concise.
translations.idiomatic: The court kept the imperial genealogy in jade registers; Liang Zhouhan had first created the system but left it incomplete. Anren thoroughly revised it and also compiled the Chart of Accumulated Blessings from the Immortal Source—both works clear in organization and concise in form.

sentences.zh: 奏置修玉牒官，事具《職官志》。

translations.literal: He memorialized to establish officials for compiling jade registers; the matter is detailed in the Offices and Ranks Treatise.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to establish posts for maintaining the imperial genealogical registers; details appear in the Treatise on Offices and Ranks.

sentences.zh: 國史成，遷右丞。

translations.literal: When the national history was complete, he was transferred to Right Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When the national history was finished, he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 是夏，又為景靈宮副使。

translations.literal: That summer, again he became vice commissioner of the Jingling Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he also served as vice commissioner of the Jingling Palace.

sentences.zh: 屢得對言事，嘗奏曰：「方今治定功成，固軼前代，陛下尚親庶政，旰食忘倦，然而君臨之大，所宜分飭有司，為式於天下。」

translations.literal: Repeatedly granted audience to speak on affairs, he once memorialized saying: "At present order is settled and achievement accomplished, indeed surpassing former ages; Your Majesty still personally attends to myriad government, eating late and forgetting weariness—yet in the greatness of sovereign rule, it is fitting to divide charge among the responsible offices and set the pattern for all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Granted frequent audiences, he once memorialized: "The realm is now peaceful and prosperous, surpassing any previous dynasty. Your Majesty still attends to every detail of government, working late without rest. Yet the burden of imperial rule is so vast that you ought to assign routine duties to the appropriate offices and set an example for the entire empire."

sentences.zh: 遂詔諸司掌常務有條例者，毋或奏稟。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued that all offices handling routine duties with established regulations should not memorialize for instructions.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed directing that departments with standing regulations for routine business should no longer submit every matter for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 天禧二年，改御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianxi, he was changed to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianxi 2 he was made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 請給御寶印，歷書三院御史彈糾事。

translations.literal: He requested provision of the imperial seal stamp and systematically recorded the impeachment and correction matters of the three censorate bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: He obtained an imperial seal for his office and recorded impeachment cases from all three censorate bureaus.

sentences.zh: 五月，暴疾卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, suddenly ill, he died, age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he died suddenly of illness, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 廢朝，贈吏部尚書，諡文定，以其子溫瑜為大理寺丞，良規為奉禮郎，承裕為正字。

translations.literal: Court was suspended; posthumously granted Minister of Civil Appointments; posthumous name Wendi; his son Wenyu made vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, Lianggui made Gentleman for Court Rites, Chengyu made Collator.
translations.idiomatic: A mourning recess was declared. He was posthumously honored as Minister of Civil Appointments with the posthumous name Wendi. His sons Wenyu, Lianggui, and Chengyu were appointed to posts as vice director of the Court of Judicial Review, Gentleman for Court Rites, and collator respectively.

sentences.zh: 安仁質直純愨，無所矯飾，寬恕謙退，與物無競，雖家人僕使，未嘗見其喜慍。

translations.literal: Anren was plain and straight, pure and sincere, without any artifice; tolerant and modest, competing with nothing; even family servants and attendants never saw him pleased or angry.
translations.idiomatic: Anren was honest, sincere, and utterly without pretense—mild, forgiving, and unassuming. Even servants in his household never saw him lose his temper or show undue excitement.

sentences.zh: 女弟適董氏，早寡，取歸給養。

translations.literal: His younger sister married the Dong clan, widowed early; he took her back to provide support.
translations.idiomatic: His younger sister had married into the Dong family and was widowed young; he brought her home to support her.

sentences.zh: 其甥董靈運尚幼，躬自訓導，為畢婚娶。

translations.literal: His nephew Dong Lingyun was still young; personally he instructed and guided him, and arranged completion of marriage.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Dong Lingyun was still a boy; Anren personally tutored him and saw him through to marriage.

sentences.zh: 幼少與宋元輿同學，元輿門地貴盛，待安仁甚厚。

translations.literal: In youth he studied with Song Yuanyu; Yuanyu's family status was noble and flourishing, treating Anren very generously.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied with Song Yuanyu, whose family was prestigious and who treated Anren with great kindness.

sentences.zh: 元輿蚤卒，家緒寢替，安仁屢以金帛濟之。

translations.literal: Yuanyu died early; the family's fortunes gradually declined; Anren repeatedly aided them with gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanyu died young and his family's fortunes waned, Anren repeatedly sent them money and gifts.

sentences.zh: 善訓諸子，各授一經。

translations.literal: Skilled at instructing his sons, to each he taught one classic.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at educating his sons, assigning each a different classic to master.

sentences.zh: 尤嗜讀書，所得祿賜，多以購書。

translations.literal: Especially fond of reading books; his salary and gifts received, much was used to purchase books.
translations.idiomatic: He loved books above all else and spent most of his salary and imperial gifts on acquiring them.

sentences.zh: 雖至顯寵，簡儉若平素。

translations.literal: Though reaching eminent favor, simple and frugal as in ordinary times.
translations.idiomatic: Even at the height of his eminence he lived as simply as he always had.

sentences.zh: 時閱典籍，手自讎校。

translations.literal: From time to time perusing classics and records, personally collating and correcting.
translations.idiomatic: He often read through his library and collated the texts by hand.

sentences.zh: 三館舊闕虞世南《北堂書鈔》，惟安仁家有本，真宗命內侍取之，嘉其好古，手詔褒美。

translations.literal: The Three Institutes long lacked Yu Shinnan's Northern Hall Book Extracts; only Anren's house had a copy; Zhenzong ordered inner attendants to fetch it, praised his love of antiquity, and personally issued an edict commendation.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Institutes had long lacked a copy of Yu Shinnan's Northern Hall Book Extracts, but Anren owned one. Zhenzong sent palace attendants to borrow it, praised his antiquarian devotion, and wrote him a personal commendatory edict.

sentences.zh: 尤知典故，凡近世典章人物之盛，悉能記之。

translations.literal: Especially knowledgeable of precedents and institutions; all the flourish of recent institutions and personages, he could entirely record them.
translations.idiomatic: He was exceptionally well versed in historical precedent and could recount in detail the institutions and notable figures of recent reigns.

sentences.zh: 喜誨誘後進，成其聲名，當世推重之。

translations.literal: Delighted to instruct and guide juniors, completing their reputations; the age esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: He delighted in mentoring young talent and helping them build their reputations, and his contemporaries held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 有集五十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collected works of fifty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings filled fifty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 溫瑜，後為國子博士。

translations.literal: Wenyu, later became Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Wenyu later served as Erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 子 良規

translations.literal: Son: Lianggui
translations.idiomatic: His son was Lianggui.

sentences.zh: 良規，字元甫。

translations.literal: Lianggui, styled Yuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Lianggui, courtesy name Yuanfu.

sentences.zh: 父安仁奏為秘書省正字、同判太常寺。

translations.literal: His father Anren memorialized to appoint him Collator in the Secretariat and concurrent vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His father Anren had him appointed collator in the Secretariat and concurrent vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 張知白薦之，召試，賜進士及第。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhibai recommended him; summoned for examination, granted jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhibai recommended him; after an examination he was granted the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 用王曙舉，擢集賢校理兼宗正丞，預修《會要》。

translations.literal: Through Wang Shu's recommendation, promoted to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and concurrent vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, participating in compiling Essentials of Governance.
translations.idiomatic: On Wang Shu's recommendation he was promoted to collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies and concurrent vice director of the Imperial Clan Court, and helped compile the Essentials of Governance.

sentences.zh: 坐宗正吏盜太廟神御物，出通判蘄州，徙河南府，知泰、滁二州。

translations.literal: Implicated because Imperial Clan clerks stole sacred imperial objects from the Ancestral Temple, he was sent out as vice prefect of Qizhou, transferred to Henan Prefecture, and governed Tai and Chu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When clerks under the Imperial Clan Court stole sacred regalia from the Ancestral Temple, he was demoted to vice prefect of Qizhou, then transferred through Henan Prefecture and served as prefect of Tai and Chu.

sentences.zh: 歷京西陝西路提點刑獄、荊湖南路轉運使，奏罷馬氏時所賦丁口米數萬石。

translations.literal: He served successively as judicial intendant of Jingxi-Shaanxi Circuit and transport commissioner of Jinghu South Circuit; memorialized to abolish the head-tax rice of tens of thousands of shi levied in Ma's time.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial intendant on the Jingxi-Shaanxi circuit and transport commissioner on the Jinghu South circuit, and memorialized successfully to abolish the head-tax grain levy of tens of thousands of shi imposed under the Ma clan.

sentences.zh: 權判三司開拆司、度支勾院，直集賢院、知廬州，積官至光祿卿，罷職。

translations.literal: Acting judge of the Opening and Inspection Office and Expenditure Audit Bureau of the Three Departments, on duty at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, governing Luzhou; accumulated offices to Court Chamberlain for Imperial Sacrifices, dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently as acting controller of the Three Departments' opening and audit offices, duty officer at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, and prefect of Luzhou, rising eventually to Court Chamberlain for Imperial Sacrifices before being removed from office.

sentences.zh: 初與張憲、掌禹錫、齊廓、張子思並為太常少卿兼館職，當進諫議大夫，而執政靳之，止遷卿。

translations.literal: At first with Zhang Xian, Zhang Yuxi, Qi Kuo, and Zhang Zisi together as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with institute duties, he should have been promoted to Supervisory Censor, but the administrators stinted it, stopping at promotion to chamberlain only.
translations.idiomatic: He had served alongside Zhang Xian, Zhang Yuxi, Qi Kuo, and Zhang Zisi as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices with an institute appointment, and was due for promotion to Supervisory Censor, but the chief ministers held back the appointment and he rose only to Court Chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 故事，卿不兼職，故皆罷。

translations.literal: By precedent, ministers did not hold concurrent posts, so all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Under established precedent, court ministers did not hold concurrent offices, and so all such posts were removed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，皆還之。

translations.literal: Before long, all were restored to them.
translations.idiomatic: Not long afterward, all were returned.

sentences.zh: 改直秘閣、同判宗正事，遷秘書監，知同、陝、相三州。

translations.literal: Changed to on-duty at the Secret Palace Hall and concurrent vice director of Imperial Clan Affairs; promoted to Director of the Secretariat; governed Tong, Shan, and Xiang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to duty at the Secret Palace Hall and made concurrent vice director of imperial clan affairs, then promoted to director of the secretariat and appointed prefect of Tong, Shan, and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 陝歲饑，百姓請閣殘稅二分，為官伐芟，以給河埽。

translations.literal: In Shan there was famine that year; the people requested deferral of two-tenths of the remaining tax and to cut wood under official orders to supply river embankments.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year in Shan, the people asked to defer two-tenths of the residual tax and supply labor for official clearing and cutting to provide for river-embankment work.

sentences.zh: 或以為須報乃可行，良規曰：「若爾，無及矣。」

translations.literal: Some thought one must report before acting could proceed. Lianggui said: "If so, it will be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Some held that approval had to be reported before anything could be done. Lianggui said, "If we wait for that, it will be too late."

sentences.zh: 檄縣遂行，而以擅命自劾。

translations.literal: He issued orders to the counties and proceeded, then impeached himself for exceeding authority.
translations.idiomatic: He sent orders to the counties and carried the plan out at once, then impeached himself for acting without authorization.

sentences.zh: 進太子賓客、權判殿中省，遷尚書工部侍郎、判本部、知濠州，卒。

translations.literal: Promoted to Honorary Attendant of the Heir Apparent and acting judge of the Directorate of Palace Services; promoted to Vice Minister of Works in the Ministry of Revenue, judge of that ministry, governing Haozhou; died.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to honorary attendant of the heir apparent and acting judge of the directorate of palace services, then to vice minister of works with charge of that ministry and appointment as prefect of Haozhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 良規所至州郡，為政不甚力，然善委任佐屬，祿賜多分贍族人，餘皆輸之酒家。

translations.literal: In the prefectures and commanderies Lianggui reached, he did not govern very vigorously, yet he was good at delegating to aides; most salary and gifts he divided to support clansmen, and the rest he paid out at wine shops.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Lianggui served, he did not push his administration very hard, but he was skilled at trusting his staff. Most of his salary and perquisites he shared among his kinsmen; whatever remained he spent at taverns.

sentences.zh: 子君錫。

translations.literal: His son was Junxi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Junxi.

sentences.zh: 孫 君錫

translations.literal: Sun: Junxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Junxi

sentences.zh: 君錫，字無愧。

translations.literal: Junxi, styled Wukui.
translations.idiomatic: Junxi, courtesy name Wukui.

sentences.zh: 性至孝。

translations.literal: By nature he was profoundly filial.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was profoundly filial.

sentences.zh: 母亡，事父良規不違左右，夜則寢於旁。

translations.literal: After his mother died, he attended his father Lianggui without leaving his side; at night he slept beside him.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother died, he waited on his father Lianggui without ever leaving his side, and at night he slept beside him.

sentences.zh: 凡衾裯薄厚、衣服寒溫、藥石精粗、飲食旨否、櫛發剪爪、整冠結帶，如《內則》所載者，無不親之。

translations.literal: Everything from bedding thick or thin, clothing warm or cool, medicine fine or coarse, food tasty or not, combing hair and trimming nails, straightening cap and tying sash—all that the Domestic Instructions prescribes—he did personally without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Whether bedding was thick or thin, clothes warm or cool, medicine fine or coarse, food savory or not, or the combing of hair, trimming of nails, straightening of cap, and tying of sash—all the duties set out in the Domestic Instructions—he performed every one himself.

sentences.zh: 及登進士第，以親故不願仕。

translations.literal: When he passed the jinshi examination, because of his parents he did not wish to take office.
translations.idiomatic: After he passed the jinshi examination, he declined office out of devotion to his parents.

sentences.zh: 良規每出，必扶掖上下，至雜立僕禦中。

translations.literal: Whenever Lianggui went out, he had to support him up and down, even when standing mixed among servants.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Lianggui went out, he had to help him up and down steps, even when they stood among the household attendants.

sentences.zh: 嘗從謁文彥博，彥博異其容止，問而知之，語諸子，令視以為法。

translations.literal: Once he accompanied him to call on Wen Yanbo; Yanbo was struck by his bearing, asked and learned the reason, told his sons, and had them take him as a model.
translations.idiomatic: Once, accompanying his father on a visit to Wen Yanbo, he so impressed Yanbo by his bearing that Yanbo asked and learned why. Yanbo then told his sons to take Junxi as their model.

sentences.zh: 良規沒，調知武強縣。

translations.literal: After Lianggui died, he was transferred to serve as magistrate of Wuqiang County.
translations.idiomatic: After Lianggui died, he was transferred to serve as magistrate of Wuqiang County.

sentences.zh: 從韓琦大名幕府。

translations.literal: He followed Han Qi in the Daming headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Han Qi's staff at the Daming headquarters.

sentences.zh: 彥博及吳充在樞管，更薦之為檢詳吏房文字，徙知大宗正丞，加秘閣校理，改宗正丞。

translations.literal: When Yanbo and Wu Chong were in the Bureau of Military Affairs, they again recommended him as examiner of documents in the Personnel Bureau; transferred to serve as vice director of the Grand Imperial Clan Court, added as collator in the Secret Palace Hall, and changed to vice director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanbo and Wu Chong served in the Bureau of Military Affairs, they recommended him again as examiner of documents in the personnel bureau. He was then transferred to vice director of the grand imperial clan court, added as collator in the Secret Palace Hall, and later made vice director of the imperial clan court.

sentences.zh: 時增諸宗院講書教授官，而逐院自備緡錢為月饋，貧者或不能以時致，宗師輒移文督取。

translations.literal: At the time lecture instructors were added to the various clan halls, but each hall had to prepare its own cash for monthly stipends; the poor sometimes could not deliver on time, and the imperial clan director would send documents to press for collection.
translations.idiomatic: At the time lecture instructors were added to the various imperial clan halls, but each hall had to supply its own cash for monthly stipends. Poorer halls sometimes could not pay on time, and the imperial clan director would send written orders to press for payment.

sentences.zh: 君錫言：「國家養天下士於太學，尚不較其費，安有教育宗室令自行束脩之理！」

translations.literal: Junxi said: "The state supports scholars throughout the realm at the Imperial Academy and still does not haggle over the cost—how can there be any principle in educating the imperial clan and making them supply their own teacher's fees!"
translations.idiomatic: Junxi said, "The state supports scholars from across the realm at the Imperial Academy and does not even quibble over the expense. How can we educate the imperial clan and yet expect them to pay their own teachers' fees!"

sentences.zh: 詔悉從官給。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that all be supplied from official funds.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that all such stipends be paid from official funds.

sentences.zh: 歷開封府推官。

translations.literal: He served as investigating magistrate of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as investigating magistrate of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，遷司勳右司郎中、太常少卿，擢給事中。

translations.literal: Early in the Yuanyou era, promoted to Director in the Right Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and elevated to Supervising Censor.
