translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanyou era he was promoted to director in the right bureau of the Ministry of Personnel and vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then elevated to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 論蔡確、章惇有罪不宜復職；

translations.literal: He argued that Cai Que and Zhang Dun, having guilt, should not be restored to office;
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Cai Que and Zhang Dun, having been guilty of crimes, should not be restored to office;

sentences.zh: 大河不可輕議東回，請亟罷修河司，以省邦費，寬民力。

translations.literal: that the Yellow River should not be lightly discussed as flowing east again; he asked urgently to abolish the River Works Office to save state expense and ease the people's burden.
translations.idiomatic: that the Yellow River must not be lightly discussed as if it could be turned east again; and he urged the immediate abolition of the river-works office to save state funds and ease the burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾出知杭州，君錫言：「軾之文，追攀《六經》，蹈藉班、馬，知無不言。

translations.literal: When Su Shi was sent out to govern Hangzhou, Junxi said: "Shi's writing vies with the Six Classics and treads upon Ban and Sima; he speaks out on whatever he knows.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Shi was sent out to govern Hangzhou, Junxi said, "Shi's writing vies with the Six Classics and treads in the footsteps of Ban Gu and Sima Qian. On whatever he knows, he speaks without reserve.

sentences.zh: 壬人畏憚，為之消縮；

translations.literal: Villainous men fear and shrink before him;
translations.idiomatic: Scheming men fear him and shrink back;

sentences.zh: 公論倚重，隱如長城。

translations.literal: public opinion relies on him, hidden like a long wall.
translations.idiomatic: public opinion relies on him as on a hidden long wall.

sentences.zh: 今飄然去國，邪黨必謂朝廷稍厭直臣，且將乘隙復進，實係消長之機。

translations.literal: Now he leaves the court lightly; evil factions will surely say the court has grown somewhat weary of upright ministers and will seize the opening to advance again—it truly bears on the ebb and flow of power.
translations.idiomatic: Now that he leaves the court so lightly, evil factions will surely say the throne has grown weary of upright ministers and will seize the opening to advance again. This truly turns on the ebb and flow of power.

sentences.zh: 不若留之在朝，用其善言則天下蒙福，聽其讜論則聖心開益，行其詔令則四方風動，為利博矣。」

translations.literal: Better to keep him at court: employ his good words and the realm receives blessing; heed his forthright counsel and the sacred mind opens and gains; carry out his edicts and the four quarters respond—the benefit would be vast."
translations.idiomatic: Better to keep him at court. Employ his good counsel and the realm would be blessed; heed his honest remonstrance and the emperor's mind would be opened and enriched; carry out his proposals and the four quarters would respond. The benefit would be immense."

sentences.zh: 進刑部侍郎、樞密都承旨，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Minister of Justice, chief conveyer of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to vice minister of justice and chief conveyer of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 即上疏勸哲宗親講學，廣諮問，為躬政之漸。

translations.literal: He immediately submitted a memorial urging Emperor Zhezong to study in person, broaden consultation—a gradual step toward personal rule.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately submitted a memorial urging Emperor Zhezong to study in person and broaden consultation, as a gradual step toward taking the reins of government himself.

sentences.zh: 君錫素有志行，後隨人低昂，無大建明。

translations.literal: Junxi had integrity and resolve by nature, but later he rose and fell with others and had no great proposals.
translations.idiomatic: Junxi had always had integrity and resolve, but later he shifted with the tide and offered no major proposals of his own.

sentences.zh: 初稱蘇軾之賢，遇賈易劾軾題詩怨謗，即繼言「軾負恩懷逆，無禮先帝，願亟正其罪。」

translations.literal: At first he praised Su Shi's worth; when Jia Yi impeached Shi for inscribing poetry of resentment and slander, he immediately followed with "Shi has betrayed favor and harbors rebellion, showed no respect to the former emperor—I wish his crime swiftly rectified."
translations.idiomatic: At first he praised Su Shi's worth. When Jia Yi impeached Shi for inscribing poems of resentment and slander, he immediately followed with, "Shi has betrayed imperial favor and harbors treasonous intent. He showed no respect to the late emperor. I urge that his crime be promptly punished."

sentences.zh: 宣仁后覽之不悅，曰：「君錫全無執守。」

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xuanren read it displeased and said: "Junxi has absolutely no steadfast principle."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xuanren read this with displeasure and said, "Junxi has no steadfast principle at all."

sentences.zh: 復以吏部侍郎、天章閣待制知鄭、陳、澶三州、河南府，徙應天。

translations.literal: Again appointed Vice Minister of Personnel, Hanlin Academician of the Heavenly Writings Pavilion, governing Zheng, Chen, and Chan prefectures and Henan Prefecture; transferred to Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed vice minister of personnel and Hanlin academician of the Heavenly Writings Pavilion, governing Zheng, Chen, and Chan prefectures and Henan Prefecture, and was later transferred to Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 因清明出郊，具奠謁杜衍、張昪、張方平、趙槩、王堯臣、蔡抗、蔡挺之塋，邀七家子孫，陪祭於側，時人傳其風義。

translations.literal: During Qingming he went out to the suburbs, fully offered sacrifices and visited the tombs of Du Yan, Zhang Bian, Zhang Fangping, Zhao Kai, Wang Yaochen, Cai Kang, and Cai Ting, invited the descendants of the seven families to join the rites at the side; people of the time spread word of his moral conduct.
translations.idiomatic: On Qingming he went out to the suburbs, made full offerings, and visited the tombs of Du Yan, Zhang Bian, Zhang Fangping, Zhao Kai, Wang Yaochen, Cai Kang, and Cai Ting. He invited the descendants of all seven families to join the rites beside him, and people of the time praised his moral conduct.

sentences.zh: 紹聖中，貶少府少監，分司南京，卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: During the Shaosheng era, demoted to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Manufactories, assigned to Nanjing in nominal capacity; died at age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng era he was demoted to vice director of the court of the imperial manufactories and assigned in nominal capacity to Nanjing, where he died at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 紹興六年，贈徽猷閣直學士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shaoxing, posthumously granted Direct Academician of the Huixian Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Shaoxing era, he was posthumously granted the title of direct academician of the Huixian Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 陳彭年

translations.literal: Chen Pengnian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Pengnian

sentences.zh: 陳彭年，字永年，撫州南城人。

translations.literal: Chen Pengnian, styled Yongnian, a native of Nancheng in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Pengnian, courtesy name Yongnian, was a native of Nancheng in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 父省躬，鹿邑令。

translations.literal: His father Shenggong was magistrate of Luyi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shenggong served as magistrate of Luyi.

sentences.zh: 彭年幼好學，母惟一子，愛之，禁其夜讀書。

translations.literal: Pengnian from youth loved learning; his mother, having only this one son, doted on him and forbade him to read at night.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Pengnian loved learning. His mother, who had only this one son, doted on him and forbade him to read at night.

sentences.zh: 彭年篝燈密室，不令母知。

translations.literal: Pengnian lit a lamp in a sealed room without letting his mother know.
translations.idiomatic: Pengnian would light a lamp in a sealed room so his mother would not know.

sentences.zh: 年十三，著《皇綱論》萬餘言，為江左名輩所賞。

translations.literal: At age thirteen he composed "Discourse on the Imperial Framework" of more than ten thousand characters, praised by renowned men of the Jiangzuo region.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he wrote the Discourse on the Imperial Framework, more than ten thousand characters long, and it won praise from leading men of the Jiangzuo region.

sentences.zh: 唐主李煜聞之，召入宮，令子仲宣與之遊。

translations.literal: The Tang ruler Li Yu heard of it, summoned him into the palace, and had his son Zhongxuan keep company with him.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler of Tang, Li Yu, heard of it, he summoned Pengnian into the palace and had his son Zhongxuan keep company with him.

sentences.zh: 金陵平，彭年師事徐鉉為文。

translations.literal: When Jinling was pacified, Pengnian took Xu Xuan as his master in writing.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinling was pacified, Pengnian studied composition under Xu Xuan.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，舉進士，在場屋間頗有雋名。

translations.literal: During the Taiping Xingguo era he passed the jinshi examination and had considerable distinction among examination halls.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo era he passed the jinshi examination and won considerable distinction in the examination halls.

sentences.zh: 嘗因京城大酺，跨驢出遊構賦，自東華門至闕前，已口占數千言。

translations.literal: Once during a great feast in the capital he rode a donkey out to compose a fu; from the Eastern Hua Gate to before the imperial gate he had already improvised several thousand characters.
translations.idiomatic: Once, during a great feast in the capital, he rode a donkey out to compose a fu. From the Eastern Hua Gate to the gate before the palace, he had already improvised several thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 然佻薄好嘲詠，頻為宋白所黜，雍熙二年始中第。

translations.literal: Yet he was frivolous and given to mocking verse, repeatedly failed by Song Bai; only in the second year of Yongxi did he finally pass.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was frivolous and fond of satirical verse, and was repeatedly failed by Song Bai. Only in the second year of Yongxi did he finally pass.

sentences.zh: 調江陵府司理參軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to judicial assistant of Jiangling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed judicial assistant of Jiangling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 因監決死囚，怖之，換江陵主簿，歷澧、懷二州推官。

translations.literal: Because he supervised the execution of condemned prisoners and was frightened by it, he was transferred to recorder of Jiangling and successively served as judicial officer in Li and Huai prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Because supervising the execution of condemned prisoners frightened him, he was transferred to recorder of Jiangling and then served successively as judicial officer in Li and Huai prefectures.

sentences.zh: 在懷，深為知州喬惟岳倚任。

translations.literal: While in Huai he was deeply relied upon by Prefect Qiao Weiyue.
translations.idiomatic: While in Huai he won the deep trust of the prefect, Qiao Weiyue.

sentences.zh: 會樊知古為河北轉運，以親嫌，徙澤州，丁內艱免。

translations.literal: When Fan Zhigu became Hebei transport commissioner, because of kinship conflict he was transferred to Ze Prefecture; when his mother died he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zhigu became Hebei transport commissioner, Pengnian was transferred to Ze Prefecture because of kinship conflict. When his mother died he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王化基薦其才，改衛尉寺丞，遷秘書郎，為大理寺詳斷官。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wang Huaji recommended his talent; he was changed to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, promoted to Secretary, and made detailed adjudication officer of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Wang Huaji recommended his talent. He was made vice director of the court of imperial entertainments, promoted to secretary, and appointed detailed adjudication officer of the court of judicial review.

sentences.zh: 坐事出監湖州鹽稅，尋又停官。

translations.literal: For an offense he was sent out to supervise the salt tax of Huzhou; soon he was again suspended from office.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was sent out to supervise the salt tax of Huzhou, and soon he was again suspended from office.

sentences.zh: 彭年素貧窶，居喪免職，賴僕人傭販以濟。

translations.literal: Pengnian had always been poor; dismissed from office while in mourning, he relied on his servant's hired trading to get by.
translations.idiomatic: Pengnian had always been poor. Dismissed from office while in mourning, he relied on his servant's hired trading to get by.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，復為秘書郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong acceded he was again made Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong acceded to the throne he was again made secretary.

sentences.zh: 喬惟岳刺史海州，及知蘇、壽二州，並表彭年通判州事。

translations.literal: Qiao Weiyue was prefect of Haizhou and also governed Su and Shou prefectures; he all memorialized recommending Pengnian as administrative vice prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiao Weiyue served as prefect of Haizhou and later governed Su and Shou prefectures, he repeatedly memorialized recommending Pengnian as administrative vice prefect.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，屢上疏言事，召試學士院，遷秘書丞、知閬州。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping he repeatedly submitted memorials on affairs; summoned for examination at the Academy, promoted to Secretary of the Secretariat and appointed prefect of Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping he repeatedly submitted memorials on public affairs. Summoned for examination at the Hanlin Academy, he was promoted to secretary of the secretariat and appointed prefect of Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，改金州。

translations.literal: Before departing, changed to Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out, his appointment was changed to Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，上疏曰：「 夫事有雖小而可以建大功，理有雖近而可以為遠計者，其事有五：一曰置諫官，二曰擇法吏，三日簡格令，四曰省冗員，五曰行公舉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he submitted a memorial saying: "Matters may be small yet able to establish great merit; principles may be near yet able to serve distant planning. There are five such things: first, establish remonstrance officials; second, select law officers; third day, simplify statutes and ordinances; fourth, reduce redundant personnel; fifth, carry out public recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he submitted a memorial saying, "Some matters are small yet can achieve great merit; some principles seem near at hand yet can serve long-range planning. There are five such matters: first, establish remonstrance officials; second, select law officers; third, simplify statutes and ordinances; fourth, reduce redundant personnel; and fifth, carry out public recommendation.

sentences.zh: 此五者，實經世之要道，致治之坦塗也。」

translations.literal: These five are truly the essential ways to order the age and the smooth path to bring governance to fruition."
translations.idiomatic: These five are truly the essential ways to order the age and the broad path to good governance."

sentences.zh: 會詔舉賢良方正，翰林學士朱昂以彭年聞，召之，辭以貧乏，請終秩。

translations.literal: When an edict called for worthy and upright men, Hanlin Academician Zhu Ang reported Pengnian; he was summoned but declined on grounds of poverty, asking to finish his term.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict called for worthy and upright men, Hanlin academician Zhu Ang reported Pengnian's name. He was summoned, but declined on grounds of poverty and asked to finish his current term.

sentences.zh: 景德初，代還，真秘閣。

translations.literal: Early in the Jingde era, when his replacement returned, made on-duty at the True Secret Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jingde era, when his replacement arrived, he was made on duty at the True Secret Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 杜鎬、刁衎薦其該博，命直史館兼崇文院檢討。

translations.literal: Du Hao and Diao Kai recommended his comprehensive learning; ordered on duty at the History Institute concurrently with collator at the Hall of Illustrious Literature.
translations.idiomatic: Du Hao and Diao Kai recommended his broad learning, and he was ordered on duty at the History Institute while also serving as collator at the Hall of Illustrious Literature.

sentences.zh: 又代潘慎修起居注，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: Also replaced Pan Shenxiu as diarist; granted vermilion robe and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: He also replaced Pan Shenxiu as diarist and was granted the vermilion robe and fish tally.

sentences.zh: 獻《大寶箴》曰：

translations.literal: He presented "Admonition on the Great Treasure," saying:
translations.idiomatic: He presented the Admonition on the Great Treasure, which reads:

sentences.zh: 二儀之內，最靈者人。

translations.literal: Within the two principles, none is more numinous than man.
translations.idiomatic: Within heaven and earth, nothing is more numinous than humankind.

sentences.zh: 生民之中，至大者君。

translations.literal: Among the living people, none is greater than the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Among the living people, none is greater than the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 民既可畏，天亦無親。

translations.literal: When the people are to be feared, Heaven also has no favorites.
translations.idiomatic: When the people are to be feared, Heaven shows no partiality.

sentences.zh: 所輔者德，所歸者仁。

translations.literal: What he relies upon is virtue; what he turns toward is benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: What he must rely upon is virtue; what he must turn toward is benevolence.

sentences.zh: 恭己禦下，輝光益新。

translations.literal: Respectful in person, governing those below, his radiance grows ever new.
translations.idiomatic: Reverent in his own conduct and gracious to those below, his radiance grows ever brighter.

sentences.zh: 載籍斯在，謀猷備陳。¤

translations.literal: The records are here; counsel is fully set forth.
translations.idiomatic: The records stand before him; every counsel is fully laid out.

sentences.zh: 內綏萬姓，外撫百蠻。

translations.literal: Within, he soothes the myriad people; without, he pacifies the hundred barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Within, he soothes the myriad people; without, he pacifies the hundred barbarians.

sentences.zh: 治亂所始，言動之間。

translations.literal: Where order and chaos begin lies between word and deed.
translations.idiomatic: Where order and chaos begin lies between word and deed.

sentences.zh: 觀之則易，處之甚難。

translations.literal: To observe it is easy; to handle it is very hard.
translations.idiomatic: To observe this is easy; to handle it is very hard.

sentences.zh: 由是先哲，喻彼投艱。

translations.literal: Therefore the ancient sages likened it to crossing hardship.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the ancient sages likened it to crossing a difficult ford.

sentences.zh: 苟能慮未，乃可防閑。

translations.literal: If one can consider what is not yet, one can guard against lapse.
translations.idiomatic: If one can consider what has not yet happened, one can guard against misconduct.

sentences.zh: 審求逆耳，無惡犯顏。¤

translations.literal: Deliberately seek words that grate on the ear; do not hate those who offend your countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberately seek words that grate on the ear, and do not resent those who offend your countenance.

sentences.zh: 既庶而富，教化乃施。

translations.literal: Once the people are numerous and rich, instruction and transformation may be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Once the people are numerous and prosperous, instruction and transformation may be applied.

sentences.zh: 慈儉之政，富庶之基。

translations.literal: A policy of kindness and thrift is the foundation of wealth and plenty.
translations.idiomatic: A policy of kindness and thrift is the foundation of wealth and plenty.

sentences.zh: 鰥寡孤獨，人之所悲。

translations.literal: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the childless—what people most pity.
translations.idiomatic: Widowers, widows, orphans, and the childless are what people most pity.

sentences.zh: 發號施令，宜先及之。

translations.literal: When issuing orders and commands, they should be applied to these first.
translations.idiomatic: When issuing orders and commands, these should be reached first.

sentences.zh: 黃髮鮐背，心實多知。

translations.literal: Yellow-haired and humpbacked elders—their minds in truth hold much knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: White-haired and bent-backed elders truly hold much knowledge in their hearts.

sentences.zh: 左右侍從，何尚於茲。¤

translations.literal: Attendants left and right—what need is there to look elsewhere?
translations.idiomatic: Attendants at one's left and right—why look elsewhere for counsel?

sentences.zh: 瞻言百辟，咸代天工。

translations.literal: Look to the hundred ministers—all stand proxy for Heaven's work.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the hundred ministers: all stand proxy for Heaven's work.

sentences.zh: 儻無虛授，可建大中。

translations.literal: If none are appointed in vain, the great Mean may be established.
translations.idiomatic: If no office is granted in vain, the great Mean may be established.

sentences.zh: 克彰慎柬，惟藉至公。

translations.literal: To make careful selection clear depends solely on utmost fairness.
translations.idiomatic: To make careful selection manifest depends solely on utmost fairness.

sentences.zh: 知人則哲，聽德則聰。

translations.literal: To know men is wisdom; to heed virtue is perspicacity.
translations.idiomatic: To know men is wisdom; to heed virtue is perspicacity.

sentences.zh: 才固難備，道亦少同。

translations.literal: Talent is hard to complete in one man; the Way also has few who share it fully.
translations.idiomatic: Talent is hard to find complete in one man, and the Way is shared by few.

sentences.zh: 葑菲罔舍，杞梓乃充。¤

translations.literal: Do not discard bracken and mugwort; then oak and catalpa may fill the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Do not discard bracken and mugwort, and oak and catalpa will fill the ranks.

sentences.zh: 不扶自直，惟蓬在麻。

translations.literal: Without support it straightens itself—only when hemp surrounds the fleabane.
translations.idiomatic: Without being propped up it grows straight—when fleabane stands among hemp.

sentences.zh: 非揀莫見，惟金在沙。

translations.literal: Without sifting none is seen—only when gold lies in sand.
translations.idiomatic: Without sifting none is seen—only when gold lies hidden in sand.

sentences.zh: 參備顧問，必辨忠邪。

translations.literal: Those who assist and advise must distinguish loyalty from treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Those who assist and counsel must distinguish loyalty from treachery.

sentences.zh: 獻替以正，裨益無涯。

translations.literal: Offer replacement to set things right; the benefit has no bound.
translations.idiomatic: Offer correction to set things right, and the benefit knows no limit.

sentences.zh: 自匿草澤，亦有國華。

translations.literal: Those who hide themselves in meadows and marshes also have the nation's flower.
translations.idiomatic: Those who hide themselves in meadows and marshes also hold the nation's finest talent.

sentences.zh: 訪此髦士，可拒朋家。¤

translations.literal: Seek such eminent scholars and cliques may be rejected.
translations.idiomatic: Seek out such eminent scholars, and factional cliques may be kept at bay.

sentences.zh: 三章之立，庶民作程。

translations.literal: When the three chapters were established, the common people had a standard.
translations.idiomatic: When the three chapters were established, the common people had a standard to follow.

sentences.zh: 欽哉恤哉，可以措刑。

translations.literal: Be reverent! Be compassionate! Thus punishment may be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Be reverent! Be compassionate! Thus punishment may be set aside.

sentences.zh: 七代之建，奸孽是平。

translations.literal: When the seven dynasties were established, villainy was leveled.
translations.idiomatic: When the seven dynasties were established, villainy was subdued.

sentences.zh: 本仁本義，可以弭兵。

translations.literal: Rooting in benevolence and righteousness, arms may be stilled.
translations.idiomatic: Rooting policy in benevolence and righteousness, arms may be stilled.

sentences.zh: 是為齊禮，亦曰好生。

translations.literal: This is aligning ritual; it is also called cherishing life.
translations.idiomatic: Thus ritual is harmonized, and this is also called cherishing life.

sentences.zh: 有教無類，自誠而明。¤

translations.literal: There is instruction without distinction of kind; from sincerity one becomes clear.
translations.idiomatic: Teach all without distinction of class; clarity comes from sincerity within.

sentences.zh: 宗廟社稷，饗之以恭。

translations.literal: Ancestral temple and state altars—feast them with reverence.
translations.idiomatic: To the ancestral temple and state altars, offer feasts with reverence.

sentences.zh: 宮室苑囿，誡之在豐。

translations.literal: Palaces, gardens, and parks—the warning lies in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: For palaces, gardens, and parks, the warning is against excess.

sentences.zh: 春鬼秋獮，不廢三農。

translations.literal: Spring hunts and autumn hunts do not cease the three field labors.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and autumn hunts must not interrupt the three agricultural seasons.

sentences.zh: 擊石拊石，用格神宗。

translations.literal: Strike stone and clap stone, thereby to arrive at the numinous ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Strike and clap the stone chimes to summon the ancestral spirits.

sentences.zh: 使人以悅，乃克成功。

translations.literal: Make people with pleasure; only then can success be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Lead the people with what pleases them, and success may then be achieved.

sentences.zh: 治國以政，罔或不從。¤

translations.literal: Governing the state by policy—none fail to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Govern the state through policy, and none will fail to follow.

sentences.zh: 濟濟多士，用之有光。

translations.literal: Full and numerous are the scholars; employing them brings brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: When scholars abound in great number, employing them lends brilliance to the realm.

sentences.zh: 硜硜小器，謀之弗臧。

translations.literal: Clang-clang small vessels—counsel for them is not good.
translations.idiomatic: Petty talents of narrow views—taking counsel from them leads nowhere good.

sentences.zh: 忠言致益，豈讓膏粱。

translations.literal: Loyal words bring benefit—how defer to fine grain?
translations.idiomatic: Loyal words bring real benefit—why yield place to pampered heirs?

sentences.zh: 六藝為樂，寧後笙簧。

translations.literal: The six arts as music—surely not placed after flutes and reeds.
translations.idiomatic: Take the Six Arts as the foundation of music, not mere pipes and reeds.

sentences.zh: 任賢勿貳，堯所以昌。

translations.literal: Employ the worthy and do not be double-minded—therefore Yao flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Employ the worthy without divided loyalty—that is how Yao brought his age to prosperity.

sentences.zh: 改過不吝，湯所以王。¤

translations.literal: Amend faults without stinginess—therefore Tang became king.
translations.idiomatic: Correct faults without reluctance—that is how Tang came to rule as king.

sentences.zh: 六合至廣，萬彙尤多。

translations.literal: The six directions are utmost broad; the myriad things are especially many.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is vast beyond measure, and the myriad creatures are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 風俗靡一，嗜欲相摩。

translations.literal: Customs and mores not uniform; appetites and desires rub against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Customs are never uniform, and appetites and desires endlessly chafe against one another.

sentences.zh: 如馭朽索，若防決河。

translations.literal: Like driving rotten rope; like guarding against a bursting river.
translations.idiomatic: It is like driving a team with rotted reins, or holding back a river about to burst its banks.

sentences.zh: 左契斯執，六轡遂和。

translations.literal: Holding the left tally, the six reins then harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: Hold firm the reins of governance, and the six teams will move in harmony.

sentences.zh: 導之以德，民免嬰羅。

translations.literal: Lead them by virtue; the people escape the infant's net.
translations.idiomatic: Guide them with virtue, and the people will be spared the snares of the law.

sentences.zh: 不懈於位，俗乃偃戈。¤

translations.literal: Not slack at one's post; customs then lay down weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Never slack in office, and the people will lay down their weapons.

sentences.zh: 先王之訓，罔不咸然。

translations.literal: The instructions of the former kings—none fail to be thus.
translations.idiomatic: The teachings of the former kings are invariably just so.

sentences.zh: 吾君之治，亦取斯焉。

translations.literal: Our lord's governance also takes this.
translations.idiomatic: Our sovereign's governance likewise takes its model from this.

sentences.zh: 小心翼翼，終日乾乾。

translations.literal: With careful care, the whole day doubly diligent.
translations.idiomatic: Cautious in every thought, diligent from dawn to dusk.

sentences.zh: 三靈降鑒，百祿無愆。

translations.literal: The three numina descend in inspection; the hundred blessings have no fault.
translations.idiomatic: When heaven, earth, and the spirits look down in approval, every blessing arrives without fault.

sentences.zh: 由茲率土，永戴先天。

translations.literal: Henceforth leading the soil, forever bearing the prior Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: From this let all within the realm forever honor the founding mandate.

sentences.zh: 巍巍洪業，億萬斯年。¤

translations.literal: Lofty and grand the great work; ten thousand myriad of years.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty and enduring is this great enterprise—may it stand for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 頃之，預修《冊府元龜》。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter, he participated in compiling the Imperial Archivum Yuan and Celestial Tortoise.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he took part in compiling the Archivum of the Imperial Archives and Celestial Tortoise.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷右正言，充龍圖閣待制，賜金紫。

translations.literal: Third year, moved to Right Rectifier of Speech, filled Longtu Pavilion Awaiting Edicts, granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to right rectifier of speech, appointed awaiting-edicts at the Longtu Pavilion, and granted the gold seal and purple robe.

sentences.zh: 先是，詔諫官、御史舉職言事，唯彭年與侍御史賈翱數有章奏，建白彈射，真宗令中書置籍記之。

translations.literal: Previously, an edict ordered remonstrance officials and censors to perform their duties and speak on affairs; only Pengnian and investigating censor Jia Ao repeatedly had memorials, establishing proposals and impeachments; Emperor Zhenzong ordered the Secretariat to set up a register and record them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, an edict had ordered remonstrance officials and censors to perform their duties and speak frankly on public affairs. Only Pengnian and investigating censor Jia Ao repeatedly submitted memorials with proposals and impeachments, and Emperor Zhenzong ordered the Secretariat to keep a register of their reports.

sentences.zh: 加刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: Added Vice Director of Penalties Branch.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to vice director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 與晁迥同知貢舉，請令有司詳定考試條式。

translations.literal: With Chao Jiong he jointly managed the tribute selection and requested that the relevant offices thoroughly establish examination regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Serving with Chao Jiong as co-director of the tribute selection examinations, he requested that the responsible offices thoroughly codify the rules for the examinations.

sentences.zh: 真宗因命彭年與戚綸參定，多革舊制，專務防閑。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong thereupon ordered Pengnian and Qi Lun to participate in fixing them; many old systems were reformed, exclusively attending to precautionary restrictions.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong thereupon ordered Pengnian and Qi Lun to revise the regulations together. They changed many old rules and focused chiefly on tightening safeguards against misconduct.

sentences.zh: 其所取者，不復揀擇文行，止較一日之藝，雖杜絕請托，然置甲等者，或非宿名之士。

translations.literal: Those they selected no longer picked literary conduct; they only compared one day's skill; though soliciting influence was cut off, those placed in the top grade were sometimes not longstanding famed scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Those they admitted were no longer chosen for literary merit and moral conduct; they judged only a single day's performance in the examination hall. Though this shut off favor-seeking, those ranked in the top grade were sometimes not established scholars of long standing.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中，議建封禪，彭年預詳定儀注，上言辨正包茅之用。

translations.literal: Mid Dazhong Xiangfu, discussion of establishing feng and shan; Pengnian participated in thoroughly fixing ritual notes, submitted words clarifying correct use of wrapped reeds.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong Xiangfu era, when the court debated performing the feng and shan rites, Pengnian helped fix the ritual protocols in detail and submitted a memorial clarifying the proper use of the wrapped reeds.

sentences.zh: 禮成，進秩工部郎中，加集賢殿修撰。

translations.literal: When ritual was complete, advanced rank to Chief Director of Works Branch, added Academician Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: When the rites were completed, he was promoted to chief director in the Ministry of Works and made an academician compiler at the Hall for Assembling Worthies.

sentences.zh: 三年，改兵部郎中、龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: Third year, changed to Chief Director of Military Branch, Longtu Pavilion Direct Academician.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to chief director in the Ministry of War and made a direct academician of the Longtu Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 遷右諫議大夫兼秘書監，詔就賜食廳編次《太宗御集》，賜勳上柱國。

translations.literal: Moved to Right Remonstrance Grandee concurrently Director of the Secretariat, edict granting use of the dining hall to compile the Imperial Collection of Emperor Taizong, granted Merit Upper Pillar of State.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right remonstrance grandee while concurrently serving as director of the secretariat. By edict he was granted the use of the dining hall to compile the Imperial Collection of Emperor Taizong, and was granted the title Merit Upper Pillar of State.

sentences.zh: 嘗因奏對，真宗謂之曰：「儒術汙隆，其應實大，國家崇替，何莫由斯。

translations.literal: Once while responding in audience, Emperor Zhenzong said to him: "The rise and fall of Confucian learning—the response is truly great; the elevation and replacement of the state—what does not proceed from this?
translations.idiomatic: Once, while answering questions in audience, Emperor Zhenzong said to him, "The waxing and waning of Confucian learning produces a vast response in the life of the state. The rise and fall of dynasties likewise proceed from nothing else.

sentences.zh: 故秦衰則經籍道息，漢盛則學校興行。

translations.literal: Therefore when Qin declined, canonical texts and the Way ceased; when Han flourished, schools were established and practiced.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin declined, the classics and the Way fell silent; when Han flourished, schools were founded and learning spread.

sentences.zh: 其後命曆迭改，而風教一揆。

translations.literal: Thereafter mandated calendars in succession changed, yet customs and teaching were one measure.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter reign titles and calendars changed in succession, yet culture and moral instruction followed a single standard.

sentences.zh: 有唐文物最盛，朱梁而下，王風寢微。

translations.literal: Tang had the most flourishing culture and institutions; from Later Liang downward, royal style gradually declined.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang, culture and institutions reached their height; from Later Liang onward, royal civilization steadily waned.

sentences.zh: 太祖、太宗丕變弊俗，崇尚斯文。

translations.literal: Taizu and Taizong greatly changed corrupt custom, honoring this refined literature.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu and Taizong radically transformed decadent customs and elevated refined learning.

sentences.zh: 朕獲紹先業，謹導聖訓，禮樂交舉，儒術化成，實二後垂裕之所致也。

translations.literal: I have obtained and continued the prior enterprise, reverently guiding the sage instructions; rites and music both raised, Confucian learning transformed into completion—truly due to the generous legacy of the two later [emperors].
translations.idiomatic: I have inherited their enterprise and faithfully follow their sage instruction. By advancing both rites and music I have brought Confucian learning to fruition—truly the generous legacy left by my two predecessors.

sentences.zh: 又君之難，由乎聽受；

translations.literal: Again, the ruler's difficulty arises from listening and accepting;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, a ruler's difficulties arise from what he hears and accepts;

sentences.zh: 臣之不易，在乎忠直。

translations.literal: The minister's not easy lies in loyalty and directness.
translations.idiomatic: A minister's hardship lies in remaining loyal and upright.

sentences.zh: 其君以寬大接下，臣以誠明奉上，君臣之心皆歸於正。

translations.literal: When the ruler with magnanimity receives those below, and the minister with sincerity and clarity serves above, ruler and minister hearts all return to correctness.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler receives his subjects with magnanimity and the minister serves his sovereign with sincerity and clarity, the hearts of both turn toward what is right.

sentences.zh: 直道而行，至公相遇，此天下之達理，先王之成憲，猶指諸掌，孰謂難哉！」

translations.literal: Walking the straight Way, meeting in utmost fairness—this is the comprehensive principle under Heaven, the completed statutes of the former kings; still pointing to the palm—who says it is hard!"
translations.idiomatic: To walk the straight path and meet one another in perfect fairness—this is the supreme principle under Heaven and the settled constitution of the former kings. It is as plain as the lines on one's palm—who can call that difficult!"

sentences.zh: 彭年曰：「陛下聖言精詣，足使天下知訓，伏願躬演睿思，著之篇翰。」

translations.literal: Pengnian said: "Your Majesty's sage words are refined and penetrating, sufficient to make all under Heaven know instruction; I humbly wish you would personally unfold your wise thought and set it forth in written compositions."
translations.idiomatic: Pengnian replied, "Your Majesty's sagely words are refined and penetrating, enough to instruct all under Heaven. I humbly hope Your Majesty will personally unfold this wise insight and commit it to writing."

sentences.zh: 真宗為製《崇儒術》、《為君難為臣不易》二論示之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong for him composed the two treatises "On Honoring Confucian Learning" and "On the Ruler's Difficulty and the Minister's Hardship" and showed them to him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong then composed two treatises for him—On Honoring Confucian Learning and On the Ruler's Difficulty and the Minister's Hardship—and showed them to him.

sentences.zh: 彭年復請示輔臣，刻石國子監焉。

translations.literal: Pengnian again requested to show the assistant ministers and carve them on stone at the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Pengnian then asked that they be shown to the chief ministers and carved in stone at the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 六年，召入翰林，充學士兼龍圖閣學士，同修國史。

translations.literal: Sixth year, summoned into Hanlin, filled Academician concurrently Longtu Pavilion Academician, jointly compiled National History.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was summoned to the Hanlin Academy, appointed academician while also serving as academician of the Longtu Pavilion, and helped compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 彭年嘗謁王旦，旦辭不見。

translations.literal: Pengnian once called on Wang Dan; Dan declined and did not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Pengnian once paid a call on Wang Dan, but Dan declined to receive him.

sentences.zh: 翌日，見向敏中。

translations.literal: Next day, saw Xiang Minzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he saw Xiang Minzhong.

sentences.zh: 敏中以彭年所上文字示旦，旦瞑目不覽，曰：「是不過興建符瑞，圖進取耳。」

translations.literal: Minzhong showed Dan the writing Pengnian had submitted; Dan closed his eyes and did not look, saying: "This is nothing but promoting auspicious portents to plot advancement."
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong showed Dan the memorials Pengnian had submitted. Dan shut his eyes and refused to read them, saying, "This is nothing but promoting auspicious portents in hopes of personal advancement."

sentences.zh: 真宗奉祀亳州太清宮，丁謂為經度制置使，以彭年副之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong performed sacrifice at the Grand Ultimate Palace in Bozhou; Ding Wei was director and disposition commissioner; with Pengnian as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong went to perform sacrifices at the Grand Ultimate Palace in Bozhou, Ding Wei served as commissioner for planning and disposition, with Pengnian as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 又與謂同知禮儀院，禮成，加給事中。

translations.literal: Again with Wei jointly managed the Court of Ritual; when ritual was complete, added Supervising Censorate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He also served with Ding Wei as co-director of the Court of Ritual. When the rites were completed, he was further appointed supervising censorate attendant.

sentences.zh: 時謂懇讓進秩，彭年亦辭之，不許，又為天書同刻玉副使。

translations.literal: At the time Wei earnestly declined advancement in rank; Pengnian also declined, not permitted; again made Deputy Commissioner for Joint Engraving of the Celestial Book Jade.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Ding Wei earnestly declined promotion in rank, and Pengnian declined as well, but neither request was granted. Pengnian was again appointed deputy commissioner for the joint engraving of the jade copy of the Celestial Book.

sentences.zh: 國史成，遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: When National History was complete, moved to Vice Director of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the national history was completed, he was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 九年，拜刑部侍郎、參知政事，判禮儀院，充會靈觀使。

translations.literal: Ninth year, enfeoffed Vice Director of Punishments, Participant in Governance, adjudicated Court of Ritual, filled Director of Assembly of Numina Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Punishments and participant in governance, placed in charge of the Court of Ritual, and made director of the Hall of Assembly of Numina.

sentences.zh: 天禧大禮，為天書儀衛副使。

translations.literal: Great rites of Tianxi, was Deputy Commissioner for Celestial Book ritual guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the great Tianxi rites he served as deputy commissioner for the celestial book ritual guard.

sentences.zh: 又為參詳儀製奉寶冊使。

translations.literal: Again was commissioner for examining and fixing ritual procedures and presenting the precious registers.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as commissioner for examining and fixing the ritual regulations and presenting the precious registers.

sentences.zh: 正月九日，侍真宗朝天書，將詣太廟，退就中書閣中如廁，眩仆，肩輿還家。

translations.literal: First month ninth day, attended Emperor Zhenzong worshipping the Celestial Book, about to proceed to the Grand Ancestral Temple; withdrew to the privy in the pavilion within the Secretariat, dizzy and fell; borne on chair returned home.
translations.idiomatic: On the ninth day of the first month, while attending Emperor Zhenzong as he worshipped the Celestial Book and was about to proceed to the Grand Ancestral Temple, he withdrew to the privy in the secretariat pavilion, grew dizzy, and collapsed. He was carried home in a sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 遣中使挾醫診療，旦夕存問。

translations.literal: Sent palace envoy bringing physician to diagnose and treat; morning and evening inquired after him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace envoy with physicians to treat him and sent inquiries morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 進兵部侍郎，表求罷奉，不許。

translations.literal: Advanced to Vice Director of Military Branch; memorial requesting dismissal from salary, not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice director of the Ministry of War, but when he submitted a memorial asking to resign his stipend, the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 二月，卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: Second month, died; age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he died, at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 真宗親臨，涕泗久之。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong personally arrived; tears flowed long.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong came in person and wept for a long time.

sentences.zh: 又睹所居陋弊，歎息數四。

translations.literal: Again seeing where he lived shabby and decrepit, sighed several times.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing how shabby his residence was, the emperor sighed again and again.

sentences.zh: 廢朝，贈右僕射，諡曰文僖，錄子佺期大理寺丞，孫彥先太常寺奉禮郎。

translations.literal: Suspend court, posthumously enfeoffed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, posthumous name Wenzhi, recorded son Qianqi as director of the Court of Judicial Review, grandson Yannian as reverent officer of the Temple of Emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Court was suspended. He was posthumously enfeoffed as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and given the posthumous name Wenzhi. His son Qianqi was granted the rank of director of the Court of Judicial Review, and his grandson Yannian was granted the rank of reverent officer of the Temple of Emperors.

sentences.zh: 真宗前後賜彭年御製歌詩凡六篇。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong before and after granted Pengnian imperial composed songs and poems in all six pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after his death, Emperor Zhenzong bestowed upon Pengnian six poems and songs composed by the imperial hand.

sentences.zh: 彭年妻入謁，出彭年像示之，錫齎甚厚。

translations.literal: Pengnian's wife entered audience; produced Pengnian's portrait and showed it; gifts very generous.
translations.idiomatic: When Pengnian's wife came to pay her respects at court, the emperor had a portrait of Pengnian brought out and shown to her, and lavished generous gifts upon her.

sentences.zh: 彭年性敏給，博聞強記，慕唐四子為文，體製繁靡。

translations.literal: Pengnian's nature quick and agile, broad learning strong memory, admired Tang four masters' literary style, form and system florid and ornate.
translations.idiomatic: Pengnian was quick-witted and agile in mind, broadly learned with a powerful memory. He modeled his writing on the four great Tang masters, and his style was florid and ornate.

sentences.zh: 貴至通顯，奉養無異貧約。

translations.literal: Noble to full display, supporting and providing no different from poor and frugal.
translations.idiomatic: Though he rose to great eminence, his household maintained the same frugal manner as in poverty.

sentences.zh: 所得奉賜，惟市書籍。

translations.literal: What he obtained from salary and grants, only used to buy books.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his salary and imperial grants on nothing but books.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符間，附王欽若、丁謂，朝廷典禮，無不參預。

translations.literal: Mid Dazhong Xiangfu, attached to Wang Qinruo and Ding Wei; court ritual codes, none he did not participate in.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dazhong Xiangfu era he attached himself to Wang Qinruo and Ding Wei, and there was scarcely a court ritual in which he did not take part.

sentences.zh: 其儀製沿革、刑名之學，皆所詳練，若前世所未有，必推引依據以成就之。

translations.literal: Ritual regulations' evolution, penal law learning—all he was thoroughly practiced in; if previous ages had not had something, he must cite precedents and rely on them to complete it.
translations.idiomatic: He was thoroughly versed in the history of ritual regulations and in penal law. Whenever something had not existed in earlier ages, he would trace precedents and draw on them until the matter was fully worked out.

sentences.zh: 故時政大小，日有諮訪，應答該辯，一無凝滯，皆與真宗意諧。

translations.literal: Therefore current affairs great and small, daily there was consultation; answering comprehensive and eloquent, entirely without stagnation—all harmonized with Emperor Zhenzong's intent.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason he was consulted daily on affairs great and small. His answers were comprehensive and fluent, never faltering, and they always matched Emperor Zhenzong's intent.

sentences.zh: 及升內閣，李宗諤、楊億皆在後。

translations.literal: When promoted to the inner cabinet, Li Zong'e and Yang Yi were both behind.
translations.idiomatic: When he entered the inner cabinet, Li Zong'e and Yang Yi still ranked ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 宗諤卒，億病退，而彭年專任矣。

translations.literal: Zong'e died, Yi sick retired, and Pengnian solely held the duties.
translations.idiomatic: After Zong'e died and Yi withdrew because of illness, Pengnian alone bore the burden of office.

sentences.zh: 事務既叢，形神皆耗，遂舉止失措，顛倒冠服，家人有不記其名者。

translations.literal: Affairs and tasks already numerous, form and spirit both exhausted; thereupon conduct and movement lost control, upside down cap and robe; family members there were who did not remember his name.
translations.idiomatic: As affairs piled up, both body and mind were worn down. He began to act erratically, putting on his cap and robes upside down, and some in his household no longer even remembered his name.

sentences.zh: 奉詔同編《景德朝陵地里》、《封禪》、《汾陰》三記，《閣門》、《客省》、《御史臺儀製》，又受詔編御集及宸章，集歷代婦人文集。

translations.literal: Received edict jointly compiling the three records Jingde Court Tombs Geography, Feng and Shan, and Fenyin; Gate, Guest Reception, and Censorate ritual regulations; again received edict compiling imperial collections and imperial compositions, collecting successive generations of women's literary collections.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he helped compile the three records on the geography of the Jingde court tombs, the feng and shan rites, and the Fenyin sacrifice, as well as the ritual regulations of the Gate Bureau, the Guest Reception Office, and the Censorate. He also received orders to compile imperial collections and imperial compositions, and to assemble anthologies of writing by women across the dynasties.

sentences.zh: 所著《文集》百卷，《唐紀》四十卷。

translations.literal: Written Collected Works one hundred volumes, Tang Annals forty volumes.
translations.idiomatic: His written works included Collected Works in one hundred volumes and Tang Annals in forty volumes.

sentences.zh: 論曰：楊礪遭遇龍飛，致位崇顯，自以夢協其兆，而忠言善政，一無可述。

translations.literal: Commentary says: Yang Li encountered dragon flight, reached position lofty and displayed; he himself took his dream as matching its omen, yet loyal words and good governance—none worth narrating.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators observe: Yang Li rose with the founding of the dynasty to eminent rank and believed his dream had foretold the omen. Yet he left nothing worth recounting in the way of loyal counsel or good governance.

sentences.zh: 惟棄官侍母，不以科名自伐，蓋有取焉。

translations.literal: Only abandoning office to serve mother, not using examination name to boast—probably had something to take from.
translations.idiomatic: Only in abandoning office to care for his mother, and in refusing to flaunt his examination honors, did he show something admirable.

sentences.zh: 宋湜懿文多識，名動人主，至與李沆同命。

translations.literal: Song Shi fine literary, much knowledge, name moved the human lord, even with Li Kang same command.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shi was a fine writer of broad learning whose reputation reached the throne, and he was appointed at the same time as Li Kang.

sentences.zh: 雖去沆遠甚，然樂善好施，士類歸之，亦可尚也。

translations.literal: Though removed from Kang very far, yet rejoicing in good and fond of giving, scholar class returned to him—also can be honored.
translations.idiomatic: Though he fell far short of Li Kang, he delighted in doing good and was generous in giving, and men of learning gathered to him—a quality still worth honoring.

sentences.zh: 王嗣宗治家能睦，為政可稱，所至立徹淫祀，亦人之所難。

translations.literal: Wang Sizong governing family able to harmonize, administering politics can be praised; wherever he arrived established abolishing excessive shrines—also what people find hard.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizong kept his household in harmony and governed well wherever he served. He abolished illicit shrines in every post he held—a feat not easily achieved.

sentences.zh: 至於剛愎少文，謀害王旦、王曾，與寇準相忤，其餘不足觀也矣。

translations.literal: As for obstinate and self-willed, little refinement, plotting harm to Wang Dan and Wang Zeng, with Kou Zhun mutually opposed—the rest not worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: But he was obstinate, uncultivated, and plotting against Wang Dan and Wang Zeng, and he clashed with Kou Zhun. The rest of his record scarcely merits attention.

sentences.zh: 李昌齡累更劇任，遂階大用，黨邪徇貨，遂貽終身之玷，良可醜也。

translations.literal: Li Changling repeatedly changed intense duties, thereupon ascended great employment; faction with the wicked, following goods—thereupon bequeathed lifelong stain—truly can be ugly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changling held one demanding post after another until he reached high office, but by allying with wicked men and trafficking in profit he left a stain that never left him—a truly shameful end.

sentences.zh: 趙安仁言事，切中時弊，及答契丹書，不失祖宗規式，又能以凶器之言折敵，不使矜戰，可謂才辨之臣矣。

translations.literal: Zhao Anren speaking on affairs, cutting to the heart of current abuses; and answering Khitan letter, not losing ancestral patterns; again able with words of ill omen to break the enemy, not letting them boast of war—can be called a talent for eloquence minister.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Anren's memorials cut to the heart of the times. In drafting the reply to the Khitan letter he preserved the forms established by the founding emperors, and with ominous language he rebuffed the enemy without letting them boast of war. He may truly be called a minister of talent and eloquence.

sentences.zh: 其孫君錫於元祐反正，論格蔡確、章惇復官之命，庶幾無忝所生。

translations.literal: His grandson Junsu at Yuanyou correction of the course, discussing rejecting Cai Que and Zhang Dun's order restoring their offices—perhaps nearly without disgracing what gave birth to him.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Junsu, during the Yuanyou restoration, spoke against the order restoring Cai Que and Zhang Dun to office—perhaps coming close to honoring the family he was born into.

sentences.zh: 陳彭年以辭藻被遇，上表獻箴，詳練儀製，若可嘉尚。

translations.literal: Chen Pengnian by literary adornment received favor, submitting memorial presenting admonition, thoroughly practiced ritual regulations—if can be praised and honored.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Pengnian won imperial favor through his literary gifts, presented admonitions to the throne, and showed mastery of ritual regulations—all of which might seem praiseworthy.

sentences.zh: 乃附王欽若、丁謂，溺志爵祿，甘為小人之歸，豈不重可歎也哉！

translations.literal: Yet attached to Wang Qinruo and Ding Wei, drowned will in rank and emolument, gladly becoming small men's follower—how is it not again heavily worth sighing!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he attached himself to Wang Qinruo and Ding Wei, drowning his ambition in rank and salary and willingly casting his lot with petty men. How greatly is that to be lamented!
